items.req: Actual use of every floor matches the occupancy group and subdivision for which the building was approved.
items.guide: Compare the occupancy certificate and approved plans with actual use, floor by floor. Record the group/subdivision (A-1 to J) per Cl. 3.1.2 to 3.1.10. A certificate of occupancy is necessary before any change in the character of occupancy.

items.req: Where occupancy has changed to a different group or subdivision, the building complies with the requirements for the new group.
items.guide: Identify changes of use since approval (e.g. storage converted to office, parking converted to shops). Compliance with the new group is not required only where the new occupancy is less hazardous (Cl. 3.1.13).

items.req: In mixed occupancy, the whole building follows the most restrictive fire protection provisions, and the occupancies are separated by 240 min fire resistance rated construction.
items.guide: Life safety provisions apply occupancy-wise; fire protection applies on the most restrictive basis. Check separating walls/floors on drawings and at site, and that egress capacity is not decreased in the direction of travel.

items.req: Additions, alterations, cubicles or partitioning have not lowered the level of fire and life safety; in high rise buildings, such work exceeding 500 m2 floor area has local fire authority approval.
items.guide: Compare as-built layout with the last approved plan. Look for added partitions that lengthen travel distance, block exits, obstruct sprinklers/detectors or breach compartment walls. Ask for the fire authority approval letter.

items.req: Valid fire safety approval / No Objection Certificate from the local fire authority is available and its conditions are complied with.
items.ref: [State / local fire service legislation (not in project files)]
items.guide: Not an NBC clause. Requirement, validity period and renewal procedure depend on the State fire service Act and rules, which are not in the project files. Record certificate number, date, validity and open conditions.

items.req: Fire and life safety audit is carried out once in two years for buildings more than 15 m in height.
items.guide: Obtain the previous audit report and its date. Check that earlier findings are closed with evidence. E-7(b): the audit should preferably be by a third party auditor with requisite experience (recommendation, not mandatory).

items.req: A qualified Fire Officer with not less than 3 years' experience is appointed and available on the premises.
items.app: Large educational complexes; business 30 m and above; residential 60 m and above; institutional 15 m and above; starred hotels; D-6
items.guide: Verify appointment letter, qualification and experience records, and the duty roster. 'Large educational complexes' is not defined in the Code; see the Ambiguities sheet. The authority may also require this for very large buildings below 30 m (Note to Cl. 4.10.2).

items.req: The Fire Officer maintains firefighting equipment, prepares and promulgates fire orders and operational plans, trains occupants, and liaises with the city fire brigade.
items.app: Where a Fire Officer is required
items.guide: Ask for the fire orders, operational plan, training attendance records and evidence of liaison (visit records, joint drills, contact list).

items.req: Fire notices/orders covering firefighting and evacuation are prepared and displayed at vantage points, and occupants are trained in their emergency actions.
items.guide: Walk each floor and check that notices are present, legible and current. Notices should be displayed prominently in bold lettering (recommendation). Interview a sample of occupants on what to do on hearing the alarm.

items.req: A written Fire Safety Plan in the Annex D format is prepared, approved by the fire authority and distributed to tenants and employees.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex D, Cl. D-5.1 to D-5.3, D-8, D-9.6]
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Check the plan against the D-8 headings: purpose, Fire Safety Director, deputies, wardens, evacuation supervisor, fire party, occupant instructions, drills, command station, signs, prevention programme, building information form, floor plans.

items.req: The Fire Safety Plan is amended and resubmitted within 30 days of any change in conditions that requires amendment.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Compare the plan revision date with the dates of tenancy changes, layout changes and system modifications.

items.req: Fire drills are conducted at least once every three months during the first two years of the building, and at least once every six months thereafter.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex D, Cl. D-3.1; NBC 2016, Part 12, Cl. 15.5, 15.13]
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (other buildings: Part 12 requires regular drills, interval not stated)
items.guide: Check the dates of the last four drills. Part 12 Cl. 15.5 and 15.13 require regular drills for all facilities but give no interval; use the Annex D frequency as the benchmark for buildings below 15 m (auditor benchmark).

items.req: All occupants participate in fire drills.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Review drill reports for participation by floor/tenant, evacuation time and lessons learnt. Occupants other than building service employees are not required to leave the floor or use the exits during a drill.

items.req: Written records of drills are kept on the premises for three years and are readily available for fire brigade inspection.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Ask to see three years of drill records.

items.req: Fire Safety Director, Deputy Fire Safety Director, a Fire Warden for each floor and Deputy Fire Wardens for each tenancy (one per 700 m2 or part thereof) are designated.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Check names against current staff. Confirm wardens know the plan, exit locations and alarm operation (D-9.3.2) by interviewing a sample.

items.req: An organization chart for fire drill and evacuation assignment is posted in a conspicuous place in each tenancy and on each floor, with a copy held by the Fire Safety Director.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Check charts at site for currency (names, contact numbers).

items.req: A Building Evacuation Supervisor is on duty at all times outside normal working hours when the building is occupied and no Fire Safety Director is on duty.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Review night and holiday rosters. Confirm the supervisor can operate the fire command centre.

items.req: A Fire Party of qualified building service employees is organized, trained and supervised.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Check the fire party list per shift, training records and practical ability (ask a member to demonstrate hose reel or extinguisher use).

items.req: An updated list of persons with physical disabilities who cannot use stairs unaided is kept, with arrangements for assisted evacuation.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Ask each floor warden for the list and the named assistants. Check that evacuation aids, refuge areas or fireman's lift procedures are defined.

items.req: Every occupant is given a Personal Fire Instruction Card with floor plan, exit routes and instructions.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Sample occupants on different floors. The card should name the assembly point and fire warden.

items.req: A plan exists for periodic formal inspection of each floor area, including exit facilities, fire extinguishers and housekeeping.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: 'Periodic' is not quantified. Auditor benchmark: monthly floor inspections with signed checklists. Review the last three months of inspection records.

items.req: Communication and alarm systems are tested monthly.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Review monthly test records for the fire alarm, public address and talk-back systems.

items.req: Signs reading 'IN CASE OF FIRE, USE STAIRS UNLESS INSTRUCTED OTHERWISE' are posted at or near every lift landing.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex D, Cl. D-4.1; NBC 2016, Part 8, Sec 5A, Cl. 7.1.1(g)]
items.guide: Lettering at least 12.5 mm block letters in red and white; sign at least 250 mm x 300 mm with stair location diagram; top of sign not above 2 m. Part 8 requires photoluminescent signs with floor plan showing stairways and direction to refuge area.

items.req: Adequate trained people are deployed to man the fire systems, with budgetary support for maintenance.
items.guide: 'Adequate' is not quantified. Check staffing per shift against the systems installed, training certificates, and the maintenance budget or contracts for fire systems.

items.req: Planned and unplanned shutdowns of fire installations are risk assessed, notified in writing to the authorities and occupants, and restored with the least possible delay.
items.guide: Ask for the impairment procedure and records of the last shutdowns. Check for any system currently isolated (valves shut, zones disabled, pumps in manual) and whether compensating measures are in place.

items.req: Records of inspection, testing and maintenance of fire systems, including hydraulic pressure tests of extinguishers, are maintained.
items.guide: Review the history sheets and service contractor reports. Cl. 15.7 additionally recommends (should) a log book of all alarms, faults, tests and periods of disconnection.

items.req: Hot work (welding, cutting, torch operations) and repair work are controlled by a permit system with fire precautions.
items.ref: [Good practice; see NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex D, Cl. D-9.8(u)]
items.guide: NBC only requires the building information form to list protective measures for alterations, repairs and torch operations. Check for a hot work permit procedure, fire watch, and removal of combustibles. Sample recent permits.

items.req: Industrial premises protected by an external hydrant system keep a trained fire squad on the premises round the clock (not less than eight trained persons at any time, or six with an automatic pressurised hydrant system), with a posted muster roll, weekly practice drills and wet drills at intervals of not more than a fortnight, recorded in a register.
items.app: Medium and large industrial risks within the scope of IS 13039
items.guide: Squad leaders to be trained by a government-recognised institution (11.2); squad issued helmets, belts and boots (11.3). During wet drills, hydrants (including those on upper floors), hoses and nozzles are used in rotation so that defects are found and corrected (11.6). The drill register, signed by the fire marshal and works manager, records attendees, dry or wet drill, hydrant numbers used, pump running time and defects (11.7). Keys of all doors available at the main gate (11.9).

items.req: The main street on which the building abuts is not less than 12 m wide, with one end joining another street not less than 12 m wide.
items.guide: Measure the clear carriageway width. Under Cl. 4.6(b) the road shall not terminate in a dead end, except for residential buildings up to 30 m height.

items.req: The approach to the building and the open spaces on all sides are not less than 6 m wide with a minimum 9 m turning radius, hard surfaced for fire tenders up to 45 t, motorable, free of obstructions and not used for parking.
items.guide: Walk the full fire tender route. Measure the narrowest point. Look for parked vehicles, landscaping, kiosks, DG sets, barriers and low cables. Check structural design of podium/basement roof slabs on the route for 45 t.

items.req: The main entrance to the plot is not less than 6 m wide, the gate folds back against the compound wall, and any built-over entrance has a clearance of at least 4.5 m.
items.guide: Measure clear gate width and height of arches, canopies or boom barriers.

items.req: Structural and non-structural elements have the fire resistance ratings required by Table 1 for the type of construction, validated and certified.
items.guide: Obtain the structural fire design basis or certificates. In their absence, Annex C gives guidance on ratings of common constructions. Note where finishes or later alterations have removed fire protection (e.g. exposed steel, cut-outs).

items.req: Load bearing steel beams and columns are protected against failure in fire where total covered area is 500 m2 and above.
items.app: Steel framed buildings, covered area 500 m2 and above
items.guide: Check for fire resistant coating, encasement or board protection and its certification; inspect for damage or missing sections (Annex C, Tables 25 and 26 are referenced by the clause).

items.req: False ceilings, including all suspension fixtures, are of non-combustible material.
items.guide: Identify ceiling material from specifications or test certificates. Look for timber framing, thermocol, plastic or fabric ceilings.

items.req: Construction is of non-combustible materials, and internal walls of staircase enclosures are of brick, reinforced concrete or other construction of minimum 120 min rating.
items.guide: Recommendation in Cl. 3.3.1; the 120 min rating for exit enclosures is mandatory through Table 1, Sl. No. (iii).

items.req: Any part of the building occupied during construction, repairs, alterations or additions has all means of exit and fire protection measures in place and continuously maintained.
items.app: Partially occupied buildings / buildings under alteration
items.guide: Check that exits serving occupied parts are not blocked by works, hoardings or stored materials, and that fire systems in the occupied part are live.

items.req: A high rise building under construction has a dry riser of minimum 100 mm with hydrant outlets and fire service inlet, 2 000 litre water drums with two fire buckets on each floor, and a water tank of minimum 20 000 litre.
items.guide: Verify physically on the constructed floors.

items.req: Temporary structures and pandals have fire precautions in accordance with good practice and a permit from the Authority.
items.guide: IS 8758 is not in the project files. Check the permit and its validity; temporary structures are permitted only in Fire Zones 1 and 2 and shall be removed on expiry of the permit (Cl. 3.2.5.2).

items.req: Each floor is compartmented so that no compartment exceeds 750 m2, or the larger limits permitted for sprinklered buildings.
items.app: All (limits for low/moderate hazard industrial and storage are set by the local fire department)
items.guide: Sprinklered limits: basement car parking 3 000 m2; other basements 2 000 m2; C-1 1 800 m2; C-2 and C-3 1 125 m2; mercantile and assembly 2 000 m2; business 3 000 m2; all others 750 m2. A minimum of two compartments is required unless the floor plate is less than 750 m2.

items.req: Compartmentation is by fire barriers with a fire resistance rating of 120 min, and penetrations are protected so that integrity is not compromised.
items.guide: Trace compartment walls above false ceilings and below raised floors. Look for unsealed cable trays, pipes and ducts, and missing wall sections above ceiling level.

items.req: Doorways or openings in fire resistant walls are limited to 5.6 m2 with maximum height/width of 2.75 m and are protected by fire doors rated not less than 120 min.
items.guide: Applies to Types 1 to 3 construction; Type 4 requires 120 min rated assemblies in openings. Measure sample openings and check door labels.

items.req: Openings in floors are protected by vertical enclosures of not less than 120 min fire resistance.
items.guide: Check stair wells, lift shafts, service risers, floor cut-outs and material hoist openings. Removable covers for machinery openings shall match the floor's strength and fire resistance (Note to Cl. 3.4.5.4).

items.req: Escalator openings have a smoke barrier of 450 to 600 mm and sprinklers on all sides of the opening on each floor.
items.guide: Measure the depth of the smoke barrier (draft curtain) around the opening and confirm the sprinkler ring.

items.req: Service ducts and shafts are enclosed with fire resistance of not less than 120 min; inspection doors of electrical shafts are rated not less than 120 min.
items.guide: Open a sample of shaft doors on several floors. Check door labels, that doors close and latch, and that shafts are not used for storage.

items.req: The space between electrical cables/conduits and the walls/slabs is filled with fire stop material rated not less than 120 min.
items.guide: Inspect floor crossings inside electrical shafts on a sample of floors (auditor benchmark: at least 10 percent of floors, and every floor with recent cabling work). The clause exempts low voltage services shafts from fire stop sealing.

items.req: Plumbing shafts in the building core that open inside the building have inspection doors rated not less than 30 min.
items.guide: Doors opening in wet areas, naturally ventilated areas or on the external wall need no specified rating.

items.req: Refuse chutes vent at least 1 m above roof level, have a non-combustible enclosure of not less than 120 min, tight fitting 60 min doors, sprinkler protection, are at least 6 m from exits and are not within stair enclosures or service shafts.
items.guide: Inspect chute hoppers on sample floors for self-closing and condition.

items.req: Fire rated doors and assemblies carry a certificate and label showing manufacturer, door type, serial/batch number, month and year of manufacture and fire resistance rating, and are certified with all hardware.
items.guide: Check labels on the door edge or frame. Look for non-rated replacement hardware, removed closers, cut vision panels, and excessive gaps (auditor benchmark: gaps as per the door's test certificate).

items.req: Fire doors to staircases, lift lobbies and pressurized spaces close automatically and completely and are kept closed.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 12, Cl. 15.3; NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex D, Cl. D-9.11]
items.guide: Open each sampled door fully and release: it should close and latch unaided. Look for wedges, hooks, tied-back closers and damaged seals. Doors held open are acceptable only on magnetic hold-open devices released by the fire alarm.

items.req: Glass is not used for enclosures of exits and exit passageways, and glazing assemblies are rated as required by Table 1.
items.guide: Check stair and exit passageway enclosures for glazed walls or panels.

items.req: In fully sprinklered buildings with fire separation of 9 m or more, the glass facade is tempered glass in a non-combustible assembly, with sprinklers within 600 mm of the facade.
items.guide: For all other buildings the facade rating follows Table 1 (Note to the clause). Check glass type from facade documents and measure sprinkler distance from the glass.

items.req: All gaps between floor slabs and the facade assembly are sealed at every level with fire resistant sealant of the same rating as the floor slab.
items.guide: Inspect the slab edge above the false ceiling or behind spandrel panels on sample floors.

items.req: Openable fire access panels are provided on each floor of a glass facade: not more than 10 m apart, operable between 1.2 m and 1.5 m above floor, not less than 1 000 mm x 1 000 mm, opening outwards and marked.
items.guide: Marking: 'FIRE OPENABLE PANEL - OPEN IN CASE OF FIRE, DO NOT OBSTRUCT' in letters at least 25 mm high on the internal side. Check that panels are in common areas and corridors, operable and not blocked by furniture.

items.req: Interior surface finishes on walls, ceilings and facade conform to the permitted flame spread class for their location.
items.guide: Class 1 may be used anywhere; Class 2 not on walls, facade, staircases and corridors; Class 3 only in living rooms and bedrooms as lining to solid walls; Class 4 shall not be used in kitchens, corridors and staircases. Ask for test certificates (IS 12777 is not in the project files).

items.req: Finishing materials and decor do not generate toxic smoke or fumes.
items.guide: No test method or limit is given in the clause; see the Ambiguities sheet. Record foam plastics, PVC panelling, synthetic drapes and similar materials on escape routes.

items.req: Battery installations are segregated by 120 min fire rated construction and ventilated as per the manufacturer's instructions.
items.app: Where battery banks / UPS rooms are provided
items.guide: Check enclosure, door rating, ventilation and absence of combustible storage.

items.req: Every exit, exit passageway and exit discharge is continuously maintained free of all obstructions or impediments to full use.
items.guide: Walk every staircase from top to discharge and every exit corridor. Record stored goods, furniture, locked or chained doors, grills, security barriers and construction material, with photographs and locations.

items.req: The number of exits is sufficient for the occupant load, the width per person and the maximum travel distance.
items.guide: Compute for each floor: occupant load (floor area / Table 3 factor, or declared number if higher), required exit width (Table 4), then check travel distance (Table 5). Record the calculation in the report.

items.req: Occupant load on each floor does not exceed the load for which the exits are designed.
items.guide: Table 3 factors (m2/person, gross): residential 12.5; educational 4; institutional 15 (indoor patients) / 10 (outdoor patients); assembly 0.65 (concentrated, no fixed seats), 1.4 (less concentrated), 1.8 (dining); mercantile 3 (street floor and sales basement), 6 (upper sales floors); business 10; industrial 10; storage 30; hazardous 10. Fixed seating: seats x 1.2. Mezzanine load is added to the floor below.

items.req: Assembly occupancies and call centres display the limiting occupant load in a conspicuous place near the entrance.
items.guide: The display should preferably be a metal plate not less than 300 mm x 200 mm with letters not less than 50 mm, giving occupancy, area and occupant load, signed by the manager.

items.req: The total capacity of the means of egress serving each floor allows egress of the entire population of the floor.
items.guide: Width per person (stairways / level components and ramps): Groups A and B 10 / 6.5 mm; Group C 15 / 13 mm; Groups D to H 10 / 6.5 mm; Group J 18 / 10 mm. Unit of exit width is 500 mm; clear widths under 250 mm are not counted. Capacity is governed by the narrowest component.

items.req: Travel distance from the most remote point to an exit does not exceed Table 5.
items.guide: Types 1 and 2 construction: 30 m for Groups A to F and H; 45 m for G-1 and G-2; 22.5 m for G-3 and J. Types 3 and 4: 22.5 m for A, B, C; 30 m for D, E, F. Values may be increased by 50 percent in fully sprinklered buildings (Note 1). Measure along the natural unobstructed path, around furniture and partitions.

items.req: Dead end corridor length in exit access does not exceed 6 m for educational, institutional and assembly occupancies and 15 m for other occupancies.
items.guide: Measure from the end of the corridor to the point where two directions of travel become available.

items.req: Exits are placed as remote from each other as possible and give direct access in separate directions from any point.
items.guide: 'As remote as possible' is not quantified; see the Ambiguities sheet for a suggested benchmark.

items.req: The building has a minimum of two staircases.
items.guide: The actual number is to satisfy Cl. 4.4.2.1. Check that both staircases are usable and independently accessible from every floor.

items.req: No alteration has reduced the number, width or protection of exits below that required.
items.guide: Compare against approved plans. Typical findings: exit doors sealed for security, stair width reduced by ducts or cupboards, exit lobbies converted to stores.

items.req: Exits can be reached without passing through another occupied unit or passage in others' control.
items.guide: Check multi-tenant floors and subdivided units for exits accessible only through a neighbour's premises.

items.req: Lifts, escalators, moving walks, turnstiles and revolving doors are not counted as exits or in egress capacity.
items.guide: Verify in the egress calculation and evacuation plan.

items.req: The capacity of the means of egress is not reduced along the path of egress travel until the exit discharge.
items.guide: Check for narrowing of stairs, doors or passageways downstream, especially at ground level discharge.

items.req: Exits and exit passageways have a clear ceiling height of at least 2.4 m and exit doors a height of at least 2.0 m.
items.guide: Measure at the lowest point, including under ducts, beams and signage.

items.req: Changes in elevation of more than 300 mm in exits use ramps or sloped surfaces with handrails and contrasting floor finish.
items.guide: Check thresholds and level changes along exit routes.

items.req: Walking surfaces in exit access are nominally level and slip resistant, with slope not exceeding 1 in 20 in the direction of travel and 1 in 48 across it.
items.guide: Steeper slopes are acceptable only where ramp requirements are met.

items.req: Turnstiles and similar devices do not obstruct required means of egress; alternative door openings of required exit width are available within 3 m and the devices disengage in an emergency.
items.app: Where turnstiles / flap barriers are installed
items.guide: Test disengagement by fire alarm signal and manually.

items.req: Access controlled exit doors, turnstiles and boom barriers automatically open in emergencies; doors unlock on fire alarm or sprinkler activation and on loss of power, and have a manual 'PUSH TO EXIT' release.
items.guide: Test a sample: simulate alarm, then isolate power to the lock. Doors shall stay unlocked until the system is manually reset. The manual release shall interrupt power to the lock directly, independent of the access control electronics.

items.req: There are no penetrations into or openings through an exit other than for fire protection piping, pressurization ducts and similar life safety services, and those are protected by passive systems.
items.guide: Look for cables, drain pipes, AC pipes and other services routed through stair enclosures and exit passageways.

items.req: At least half of the required exit stairs from upper floors discharge directly to the exterior or through exit passageways.
items.guide: The remaining stairs may discharge through a large lobby. Check that discharge points lead to open space or a street and are not blocked.

items.req: Corridors and passageways used for exit access are not narrower than the calculated exit width.
items.guide: Measure clear width at the narrowest point, including at door swings and columns.

items.req: Tables, chairs and other temporary or permanent structures are kept out of exit access corridors.
items.guide: The clause says such objects 'shall be avoided'. Record waiting chairs, vending machines, display racks, photocopiers and lockers in corridors.

items.req: Exit access does not pass through storage rooms, closets or similar spaces.
items.guide: Follow each exit route from the most remote room.

items.req: Exit access to the fireman's lift and refuge area is step free and signposted with the international symbol of accessibility.
items.app: Where fireman's lift / refuge area is provided
items.guide: Check for raised thresholds and steps on the route.

items.req: Exit doorways are not less than 1 000 mm wide (2 000 mm in assembly buildings) and not less than 2 000 mm high.
items.guide: Measure clear opening width with the door open at 90 degrees.

items.req: Doors in exits open in the direction of exit, are not overhead or sliding doors, and do not obstruct the stair landing.
items.guide: In Group D and C-1 the exit door shall not open directly onto a flight of stairs. In other occupancies the open door shall not reduce the landing pathway by more than half the stair width.

items.req: Exit doorways are operable from the side they serve without the use of a key.
items.guide: Try every exit door on the sampled floors from the egress side, including final exit doors at ground and terrace doors. Record padlocks, key-operated locks and break-glass key boxes.

items.req: Mirrors are not placed on exit doors or in exits.
items.guide: Visual check.

items.req: Revolving doors forming part of a means of egress collapse to a book-fold position with egress paths not less than 1 000 mm, are not within 3 m of stairs or escalators, and have a hinged door of the same capacity in the same wall within 3 m.
items.guide: Each revolving door is credited with only 50 persons.

items.req: Doors in folding partitions are not treated as means of egress.
items.guide: Check banquet halls, conference rooms and training rooms.

items.req: Staircase widths are not less than the minimum for the occupancy.
items.guide: Minimum width: A-2 1.00 m; A-1, A-3 and A-4 1.25 m; A-5 and A-6 1.50 m; assembly 2.00 m (1.50 m where less than 150 persons); educational 1.50 m; institutional 2.00 m; all other occupancies 1.50 m. Measure clear width between wall and handrail side as built.

items.req: Treads are at least 250 mm (residential) or 300 mm (other buildings), risers do not exceed 190 mm (A-2) or 150 mm (other buildings), there are not more than 12 risers per flight, and treads are non-slip.
items.guide: Measure a sample of flights in each staircase. Tread is measured without nosing.

items.req: Internal staircases are of non-combustible construction with a fire resistance rating of minimum 120 min, and access to them is through fire doors of minimum 120 min rating.
items.guide: Check enclosure continuity on every floor, door labels, and that doors are self-closing.

items.req: No staircase is arranged around a lift shaft, and lifts do not open into the staircase.
items.guide: Visual check against plans.

items.req: No flue, electromechanical equipment, air conditioning unit, gas piping, electrical panel, electrical shaft or air conditioning duct is in, passes through or opens into the stairway.
items.guide: Inspect each staircase full height, including under-stair spaces and landings.

items.req: No living space, store or other fire risk opens directly into a staircase, and no combustible material is used for decoration or wall panelling in the staircase.
items.guide: Record stores under stairs, meter cupboards, security cabins and notice boards with combustible backing.

items.req: Staircases are not used as part of a supply, return or exhaust air system, and there are no openings in walls or doors separating exits from adjoining areas.
items.guide: Check for transfer grilles, louvres or undercut doors between the stair and the floor.

items.req: Handrails are provided on one side of stairs less than 1 500 mm wide and on both sides of stairs 1 500 mm and wider.
items.guide: The Code is inconsistent on permitted handrail projection: item (f) says not more than 115 mm, item (g) says not more than 90 mm. Use 90 mm as the conservative benchmark and note the inconsistency.

items.req: Headroom under landings and stairs is at least 2.2 m, and beams, columns or other features do not reduce the headroom or width of the staircase.
items.guide: Measure at the lowest projection.

items.req: Exit staircases are continuous from the refuge floor or terrace to the level of exit discharge, terminate at that level, and the basement is served by a separate staircase.
items.guide: Check that the upper-floor stair does not continue down to the basement without separation at the discharge level.

items.req: A floor indication board (not less than 300 mm x 200 mm) showing staircase number, floor number and direction to exit discharge is fixed inside each staircase near the fire door, and floors are indicated on the wall outside the staircase.
items.guide: Annex D (high rise) requires floor numerals at least 75 mm high in contrasting colour on the stair side of the door.

items.req: Scissor type staircases and curved stairs are not counted as exits.
items.guide: Curved stairs may serve exit access only if tread depth is at least 280 mm at 350 mm from the narrow end and the smallest radius is at least twice the stair width.

items.req: External staircases are kept in sound and usable condition, are directly connected to the ground, and have an entrance separate and remote from the internal staircase.
items.guide: Check for corrosion, loose treads, missing balusters, locked gates at ground and storage on landings.

items.req: External stairs are of non-combustible construction, doorways leading to them have at least 120 min fire resistance, and wall or window openings within 3 m are protected by assemblies rated at least 60 min.
items.guide: Measure the distance to the nearest unprotected opening, including AC outdoor units and exhaust louvres.

items.req: External stairs are inclined at not more than 45 degrees, have straight flights not less than 1 500 mm wide, and handrails on both sides 1 000 to 1 200 mm high with balusters at maximum 150 mm gap.
items.guide: Measure.

items.req: Spiral staircases are used only for low occupant load in buildings not exceeding 9 m in height and are not less than 1 500 mm in diameter.
items.guide: 'Low occupant load' is not quantified; see the Ambiguities sheet.

items.req: Ramps used for egress have a slope not exceeding 1 in 12, slip resistant surface without perforations, landings at top, bottom, doors and changes of direction (1.5 m x 1.5 m), and handrails on both sides.
items.guide: These requirements do not apply to basement car parking ramps (Note to the clause).

items.req: Every basement has not less than two independent exits, sized for the actual occupancy of the basement.
items.guide: A ramp is not counted as an exit for car parking basements below the first basement (Table 5, Note 2).

items.req: Where a basement car park has direct approach from an occupancy above, the door openings to the basement are protected by 120 min fire doors.
items.guide: Exit discharge doors from the basement are excepted. Check lift lobby and stair doors at basement levels.

items.req: Exit access, exits and exit discharge are illuminated continuously at all points, including corridors, stairwells and landings.
items.guide: Walk the routes with normal lighting on; note failed lamps and dark stretches.

items.req: Emergency lighting is powered from a source independent of the normal lighting supply.
items.guide: Identify the source (generator, central battery, self-contained luminaires) from the single line diagram.

items.req: Horizontal illuminance at floor level on the centreline of escape routes is not less than 10 lumen/m2 (10 lux) under emergency lighting.
items.guide: Measure with a calibrated lux meter with normal lighting switched off. For routes up to 2 m wide, 50 percent of the width shall have at least 5 lux. In auditoria and theatres, exit access illumination may be reduced to not less than 2 lux during performances.

items.req: Failure of any single lighting unit does not leave any area of the escape route in darkness.
items.guide: Check luminaire spacing and circuiting.

items.req: Emergency lighting comes on within 5 s of failure of the normal supply and maintains the required illumination for not less than 90 min.
items.guide: Simulate mains failure on a sample circuit and time the changeover. For duration, review the last full-duration discharge test record or witness a test.

items.req: Battery pack emergency lighting is not used in lieu of a diesel engine driven emergency power supply.
items.guide: Under Cl. 3.4.7.2 the alternative supply for exit passageway and staircase lighting may be a battery continuously trickle charged from the mains; read the two clauses together and record the arrangement found.

items.req: Escape lighting luminaires are located near corridor intersections, exits and exit doors, changes of direction and level, each staircase flight, final exits, fire alarm call points and firefighting equipment, and are mounted at least 2 m above floor level.
items.guide: Locations are a recommendation ('should'); the 2 m mounting height is mandatory. 'Near' means within 2 m horizontally (Note to the clause).

items.req: Exit passageway (at ground) and staircase lighting is connected to an alternative supply.
items.guide: Verify by switching off the normal supply.

items.req: Double throw switches prevent staircase and corridor lighting from being connected to two sources of supply simultaneously.
items.guide: Check in the service room where the standby supply terminates.

items.req: The emergency lighting system is maintained by periodical inspections and tests.
items.guide: 'Periodical' is not quantified. Auditor benchmark: monthly functional test and annual full-duration (90 min) test, with records.

items.req: No point in an exit access is more than 30 m from a visible exit directional sign, and a directional sign is provided at every change in direction.
items.app: All (not applicable to A-2 and A-4 below 15 m)
items.guide: Walk the routes from the most remote points.

items.req: Exit signs are green, illuminated, and wired to an independent circuit on an alternative source of supply.
items.app: All (not applicable to A-2 and A-4 below 15 m)
items.guide: Sizes and colours follow good practice [4(7)], which is not in the project files. Check signs stay lit on mains failure. Signs should be installed so that furniture or equipment movement cannot damage them.

items.req: Photoluminescent markings are provided at internal hydrant boxes, and firefighting equipment is marked by luminous signs.
items.guide: Visual check with lights off where practicable.

items.req: Each stairway and lift bank is identified by a letter sign, and stair re-entry signs are posted on each floor within each stairway.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex D, Cl. D-4.3, D-4.4]
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Re-entry sign lettering at least 12.5 mm, fixed approximately 1.5 m above floor level.

items.req: Staircases and lift lobbies are pressurized or naturally/cross ventilated as required by Table 6 for the building height.
items.guide: Internal staircase without external wall: pressurized at all heights (except A-2 and A-4 below 15 m). Staircase with external wall: natural ventilation or pressurization (cross ventilation or pressurization above 30 m). Lift lobby: not required below 15 m at ground and above, but segregation and pressurization are required for lifts travelling from ground to basement. Enclosed staircases serving more than one basement shall be pressurized (Note 2).

items.req: Pressure difference is 50 Pa for staircases and between 25 Pa and 30 Pa for lobbies or corridors.
items.guide: Witness a test with fans running and all doors closed; measure with a calibrated differential pressure gauge at top, middle and bottom. Review commissioning and periodic test reports. Where no lift lobby can be provided, the lift hoistway is pressurized at 50 Pa.

items.req: Naturally ventilated staircases have an opening of 0.5 m2 in the external wall at each landing; cross ventilated staircases have two such openings in opposite or adjacent walls.
items.guide: Measure openings; check they are not glazed shut, boarded or blocked.

items.req: Stair pressurization is initiated by a signal from the fire alarm panel and is integrated with and supervised by the fire alarm system.
items.guide: Simulate an alarm and confirm automatic fan start and status indication at the fire command centre.

items.req: When pressurization operates, air recirculation stops, exhaust air is vented to atmosphere and air supply to spaces other than exits stops.
items.guide: Verify the cause and effect matrix and witness a test.

items.req: Pressurized staircases are segregated from unpressurized areas by 120 min fire resistant walls, and the fresh air intake is at least 4 m from any exhaust outlet.
items.guide: Measure the intake to exhaust separation at roof or plant level.

items.req: In buildings greater than 60 m, pressurization is evaluated so that the force to set a stair door leaf in motion does not exceed 133 N.
items.guide: Recommendation ('it is recommended'). Measure door opening force with a force gauge while fans are running.

items.req: Exit access corridors of guest rooms, indoor patient areas and sleeping accommodation have 60 min fire resistant walls and 20 min self-closing fire doors, with a smoke exhaust or pressurization system.
items.app: Hotels, hospitals, apartments, custodial, penal and mental institutions
items.guide: Not required for naturally cross ventilated corridors or corridors with operable windows. Smoke exhaust is also required for theatres/auditoria and large lobbies.

items.req: Exit passageways from exit to exit discharge are pressurized or naturally ventilated, with 120 min fire doors; mechanical pressurization is automatic with additional manual controls.
items.guide: Check doors, integrity of the passageway and controls.

items.req: Smoke exhaust systems provide a minimum of 12 air changes per hour, and smoke exhaust fans are rated 250 deg C for 120 min.
items.guide: Check fan nameplates/certificates and the air balance report (design flow / volume served).

items.req: Each basement is separately ventilated, by vents of aggregate area not less than 2.5 percent of floor area spread around the perimeter, or by mechanical ventilation giving 12 air changes per hour in fire.
items.guide: In multi-level basements, supply and exhaust fans are in 120 min fire resisting rooms and exhaust fans have back draft dampers to the common shaft.

items.req: The basement smoke extraction system operates on sprinkler flow switch actuation, has local and/or remote manual start-stop control for fire fighters, and gives visual indication of fan status.
items.guide: Simulate flow switch operation; test the manual control.

items.req: Power supply panels for smoke ventilation fans are in a fire safe zone and cabling meets circuit integrity requirements.
items.guide: Check cable type marking and routing. IS 16246 is not in the project files.

items.req: Smoke ventilation systems do not cross transformer areas, electrical switchboards, electrical rooms or exits; supply air intake is not less than 5 m from exhaust discharge; inlets and outlets at ground are marked 'AIR INLET' / 'SMOKE OUTLET'.
items.guide: Marking of stall board and pavement lights is a recommendation ('should').

items.req: Separate air handling units serve each floor, and air ducts of one floor do not interconnect with ducts of any other floor.
items.guide: A separate AHU for each compartment within a floor is desirable (advisory).

items.req: Air handling units have smoke sensitive devices that prevent circulation of smoke through the system.
items.guide: Test AHU trip on duct/return air smoke detector actuation or fire alarm signal.

items.req: AHU air filters are of non-combustible material and AHU rooms are not used to store combustible material.
items.guide: Inspect each AHU room.

items.req: Air ducts do not pass through exits, exit passageways or exit enclosures, and exits and lift lobbies are not used as return air passages.
items.guide: Check above ceilings at stair and lobby walls.

items.req: Fire or fire/smoke dampers are provided where ducts cross fire separation walls and floors and enter vertical shafts, and openings around ducts are sealed to the rating of the compartment.
items.guide: Dampers may be omitted only in ducts required for fire safety operation, which shall then have 120 min integrity. Ducts within a compartment need a minimum 30 min rating (Cl. 3.4.8.3.4).

items.req: Dampers are motorized or fusible link type, accessible for maintenance and testing, integrated with the fire alarm panel, and have manual operation facilities.
items.guide: Operate a sample of dampers from the panel and manually; check access panels (Cl. 3.4.8.3.6).

items.req: Duct insulation, inside or outside, is non-combustible and not wrapped or secured with combustible material.
items.guide: Check material certificates and inspect samples.

items.req: Smoke extraction fans, pressurization fans and fire dampers are periodically run and tested and kept maintained.
items.guide: The clause says at least a fortnightly check is desirable. Review run/test logs for the last three months.

items.req: The electrical installation follows good practice for fire safety and Part 8 Section 2 of the Code.
items.guide: The clause says 'reference may be made'. Cross-refer to the electrical safety audit. Flame retardant wiring is described as desirable. IS 1646 is not in the project files.

items.req: Medium and low voltage wiring in shafts and within false ceilings runs in metal conduit, and 230 V wiring above false ceilings has 660 V grade insulation.
items.guide: Open ceiling tiles at sample locations. Record loose wiring, PVC conduit and open joints above ceilings.

items.req: Electric distribution cables and wiring are in a separate shaft that is sealed at every floor with fire stop material of the same fire resistance as the floor.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Cl. 3.4.6.1; CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 38(3)(iii)]
items.guide: Inspect electrical shafts on sample floors. CEA Reg. 38(3)(iii) requires a fire barrier at each floor crossing of every power cable and service duct in buildings above 15 m and public buildings.

items.req: Water mains, gas pipes, telephone, intercom or any other service lines are not laid in the duct for electrical cables.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Cl. 3.4.6.1; CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 38(3)(iii)]
items.guide: Use of bus ducts or solid rising mains instead of cables is preferred (advisory). CEA Reg. 38(3)(iii) also prohibits other service pipes and cables in power cable ducts.

items.req: High, medium and low voltage wiring in shafts and false ceilings runs in separate shafts or conduits.
items.guide: Visual check.

items.req: Cables for fire alarm and public address systems are in metal conduit or armoured, segregated from power cables.
items.guide: Visual check in shafts and above ceilings.

items.req: All metallic items such as steel structural members are bonded to the earthing system.
items.guide: Cross-refer to the electrical safety audit (earth continuity tests).

items.req: Emergency system circuits are protected at origin by an automatic circuit breaker with its no-volt coil removed, and master switches controlling essential service circuits are clearly labelled.
items.guide: Check at the main and emergency panels.

items.req: Normal and emergency (standby generator) power with changeover is provided to: fire pumps; pressurization and smoke venting; fireman's lifts (including all lifts); exit signage; emergency lighting; fire alarm; PA system; magnetic door hold-open devices; fire command centre and security room lighting.
items.guide: Trace each system on the single line diagram. Witness a changeover test where possible. The generator may be waived by the Authority where a parallel supply from a separate substation on a different grid is provided.

items.req: The generator is capable of taking the starting current of all fire and life safety systems and equipment.
items.app: Where a standby generator is provided
items.guide: Review the load calculation; check loads added since design.

items.req: Power to fire and life safety panels is through fire proof enclosures, circuit integrity cables or an alternate route through the adjoining fire compartment, and the panels are in a fire safe zone.
items.guide: Check cable type and routing from the essential panel to the fire pump, lift, pressurization and alarm panels.

items.req: Substation areas are not used for storage or any other utility purpose.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Cl. 3.4.6.3; CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 51(i)]
items.guide: The substation should be adequately ventilated (recommendation).

items.req: An independent ventilated or air conditioned MV panel room is provided at ground level or first basement, with access from outside and 120 min fire resistant walls and doors.
items.app: Where an MV panel room is provided
items.guide: Visual check; door label.

items.req: Electrical MV main distribution panel and lift panels have CO2/inert gas flooding for all panel compartments, with a cylinder beside the panel.
items.guide: Check cylinder pressure/weight, discharge tubing into each compartment and service tags.

items.req: Meter rooms on upper floors do not open into staircase enclosures.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Cl. 3.4.6.3; CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 38(3)(viii)]
items.app: Where meter rooms are on upper floors
items.guide: They should be ventilated directly to open air or located in an electrical room with 120 min walls (recommendation). CEA Reg. 38(3)(viii) adds that the electricity meter is not installed in the passage of a staircase.

items.req: Oil filled substation equipment is in a utility building or outdoors, at least 7 m from adjoining buildings; equipment exceeding 2 000 litre oil has 240 min baffle walls; transformers exceeding 10 MVA have high velocity water spray or nitrogen injection.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Cl. 3.4.6.3.1, 5.1.4 [IS 15325; CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 46(2)(vi), (vii), (ix)]
items.app: Where oil filled equipment is installed
items.guide: Baffle walls extend at least 600 mm above the equipment (including conservator) and 300 mm beyond each side. Measure.

items.req: Transformers inside the building are dry type, in a substation/switch room with 120 min fire resistance to walls, ceiling, floor and doors, with access from the nearest fire exit or exit staircase.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Cl. 3.4.6.3.2; CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 46(2)(x), (xii)]
items.app: Where transformers are inside the building
items.guide: Check nameplate and enclosure. CEA Reg. 46(2)(xii) also requires dry type transformers only inside residential and commercial buildings; for basement substations CEA Reg. 46(2)(x) requires 4 h walls (see P-45 and Ambiguities).

items.req: Diesel generator sets are installed only at ground floor or first basement, in a room separated by 120 min fire rated walls and doors, with ventilation and exhaust planned.
items.guide: Visual check; door label; exhaust routing.

items.req: The DG oil tank (if not in the base of the DG) has a dyked enclosure of at least 10 percent more than the tank volume, filled with sand to a height of 300 mm.
items.app: Where a separate DG fuel tank is provided
items.guide: Measure the dyke; check for stored oil drums outside the dyke. The Petroleum Act, 1934 and Rules (not in project files) apply to petroleum storage.

items.req: Lightning protection down conductors are not routed through electrical or other service shafts.
items.guide: Trace down conductors from roof to earth pits.

items.req: Where transformers are at higher floors, HT cables are routed through a separate shaft with its own 120 min fire resistance rating.
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) with transformers at upper floors
items.guide: E-5 also requires compliance with Part 8 Section 2 and Section 7 of the National Electrical Code 2011 (NEC is not in the project files).

items.req: Manually operated electronic fire alarm and automatic detection and alarm systems are provided as required by Table 7 for the occupancy, height and area.
items.guide: Identify the applicable row of Table 7 for the building and record 'R' / 'NR' for each system in the report. Check coverage on every floor, including plant rooms, stores and above deep false ceilings.

items.req: The fire detection system is in accordance with accepted standards, and detector selection, installation and maintenance follow good practice.
items.guide: Verify detector selection, zoning, siting, wiring and maintenance against IS 2189 : 2008 using items H-14 to H-25. Review the design, as-built drawings and commissioning certificate; every detector is to be tested after installation (IS 2189, Cl. 7.2).

items.req: The alarm system includes talk-back and public address systems where required.
items.app: Occupancies listed in Note 1; all buildings 15 m and above (24 m and above for A-3 and A-4); car parking over 300 m2 and multi-level car parking
items.guide: Test talk-back from a sample of floors to the fire command centre, and PA audibility on each floor.

items.req: Voice evacuation uses pre-recorded messages in Hindi, English and the vernacular language and is integrated with the fire alarm panels to alert the fire zone and surrounding zones.
items.guide: Trigger a test message; check intelligibility and zoning.

items.req: Visual strobes/beacons are provided for persons with hearing impairment.
items.guide: Advisory ('may be considered'). Record where provided and working.

items.req: Detectors are provided inside electrical shafts and lift machine rooms in addition to occupancy areas.
items.app: Assembly and institutional buildings; all buildings above 30 m with fire alarm per Table 7
items.guide: Open sample shafts and check.

items.req: Fire alarm panels are connected in a peer to peer network or by redundant cables run in different shafts, and each panel can work in standalone mode.
items.guide: Review the network architecture drawing; simulate a network break if the maintainer agrees.

items.req: The fire alarm panel monitors water level in all tanks, hydrant and sprinkler pressures, pump ON/OFF status and all isolation valves fitted with supervisory switches.
items.guide: Check each signal on the panel or graphics; operate a supervised valve and confirm the signal.

items.req: The fire alarm system operates the interfaced systems: air handling units, pressurization, smoke management, fire dampers, release of hold-open fire doors, access control release and lift grounding.
items.guide: Obtain the cause and effect matrix and witness a test of each interface. Cl. 4.9(b) says the systems 'may include' these items; individual interfaces are mandatory under their own clauses.

items.req: The fire panel is checked every day for normal operation, faults are logged with corrective action, and the control panel is manned regularly.
items.app: Where a fire alarm panel is provided
items.guide: Look at the panel now: record standing faults, disabled zones or devices and silenced sounders. Review the daily log for the last month.

items.req: Fire detection systems are maintained in accordance with good practice, and no detector is painted, covered or altered during fit-out or refurbishment.
items.guide: Look for painted detectors, dust covers left on, detectors removed for interior work, and detectors blocked by partitions or storage. IS 2189 prohibits painting or altering detectors and requires a clear space of 500 mm below each detector (Cl. 6.3.2); the quarterly check uses a 750 mm radius (Cl. 7.4.5(f)); see Ambiguities. Heavily painted detectors are to be replaced.

items.req: A log book records all alarms (genuine, test or false), faults, service tests, routine inspections and periods of disconnection.
items.app: Where a fire alarm system is provided
items.guide: Recommendation ('should'). Review false alarm frequency and causes.

items.req: In car parking areas, detection is provided in electrical rooms, cabins and other areas even where not required in the parking area itself.
items.guide: Visual check.

items.req: Manual call points are located so that no person travels more than 30 m (45 m outside the building) to reach one, preferably near staircase entries on each level, at 1.4 m above floor, conspicuous, well lit and unobstructed.
items.app: Where a fire alarm system is provided
items.guide: Measure travel to the nearest call point on sampled floors; reduce the distance where access is difficult or the risk is high. In long corridors call points are surface or semi-recessed to show a side profile of at least 750 mm2. Break-glass: glass area at least 30 cm2, not more than 2 mm thick, in a dust and moisture-proof enclosure. Operate a sample (auditor benchmark: at least one per zone on sampled floors); the alarm must sound on the floor and at the panel and stay latched until reset. Sounder levels: see H-15.

items.req: Alarm sounders produce at least 65 dB(A), or 5 dB(A) above any background noise likely to persist for more than 30 s, whichever is greater, at every occupiable point; at least 75 dB(A) at the bed-head (doors shut) where occupants sleep; and at least one sounder is provided in each fire compartment.
items.app: Where a fire alarm system is provided
items.guide: Measure with a sound level meter during the alarm test at worst-case points (rooms behind doors, plant rooms, toilets, noisy work areas). Sounder frequency 500 to 1 000 Hz, signal continuous. A single door attenuates more than 20 dB, so a room separated from the nearest sounder by more than one wall or door is unlikely to be satisfactory. Levels above 120 dB(A) in occupied areas may damage hearing. Many quieter sounders are preferred to a few very loud ones.

items.req: Detection zones allow a fire to be located quickly: zone floor area not more than 2 000 m2; each zone confined to one floor where the building exceeds 300 m2; search distance within a zone not more than 30 m; and zone boundaries follow fire compartment boundaries.
items.app: Where automatic detection is provided (zone indication is needed even on addressable systems, Cl. 4.2.1(b))
items.guide: Compare the zone chart at the panel with the floor plans. Also check: detectors in enclosed stairwells, lift wells and shafts form separate zones; call points on stair landings belong to the zone of the adjoining floor; no zone covers more than one occupancy in multi-tenant buildings; no zone extends into parts of two compartments (Cl. 4.2.2, Note 2). Special risks within a large area are separate zones. Conventional zones: not more than 20 detectors per zone (Cl. 4.1.2).

items.req: Point detectors are sited so that, under flat ceilings, no point is more than 7.5 m from the nearest smoke detector or 5.3 m from the nearest heat detector, with spacing reduced for ceiling height and high air movement, and detectors kept clear of walls, beams and air inlets.
items.guide: Height (Cl. 6.3.3(a)): smoke detectors at 7.5 m apply up to 7 m ceiling height, 5 m for 7 to 10 m, beam or aspirating detection only above 10 m; heat detectors at 5.3 m up to 5 m height, 3.5 m for 5 to 7 m, not permitted above 7 m. Reduce spacing per Table 2 where air changes exceed 7.5 per hour. Cross-check: at least one smoke detector per 100 m2 or heat detector per 50 m2. Siting: not within 500 mm of walls or of beams/ducts deeper than 250 mm; not within 1 m of air inlets and 1.5 m of supply diffusers; beams deeper than 10 percent of ceiling height, and racks or partitions within 300 mm of the ceiling, create separate enclosures. Sensing element 25 to 600 mm below ceiling for smoke, 25 to 150 mm for heat (Cl. 6.2).

items.req: Detectors are provided in every room and cabin (at ceiling level and in the false ceiling void where required), at the top of every stairwell, lift shaft and utility shaft, in lift machine rooms, at each main landing of unenclosed stairs, and in cable tunnels, ducts, false floors, AC and AHU rooms, long return-air ducts and distribution boards.
items.guide: False ceiling or floor voids deeper than 800 mm need detectors at normal spacing; shallower voids only where fire products can spread between rooms through the void. Toilets and WCs need not be covered. Where a floor has several enclosed rooms, and for concealed detectors in voids, shafts and tunnels, remote response indicators are required at the entrance. A detector on the protected side 1.5 m from any opening into an unprotected area.

items.req: Detector types suit the risk and environment: smoke detection on escape routes and in air-conditioned, slow-burning or life-safety areas; heat detectors limited to areas where smoke, steam or dust occur in normal use (for example kitchens, pantries, DG and boiler rooms).
items.guide: Cl. 5.2: the system shall have detectors suited to the conditions that give the earliest reliable warning. Cl. 5.2.1.1: heat detectors are not suitable in slow-burning or air-conditioned premises where escape routes may be smoke-logged first. EDP and computer rooms: smoke detection (5.2.2.1); archives and museums: combined heat, smoke and flame (5.2.2.2). Ionisation detectors are discouraged (Note to Cl. 3.45). Annex A is guidance. Record heat detectors on corridors, lobbies and other escape routes as a finding.

items.req: Fire alarm cables and equipment are independent of all other systems; addressable loops are wired Class A (return loop) with short-circuit isolators, and loops are not loaded beyond about 90 percent of their capacity.
items.app: Where a fire alarm system is provided
items.guide: Cl. 4.2.4: loop length not more than 3 000 m with conductor of at least 1.5 mm2 (or the manufacturer's limits); not more than 8 fire zones per loop; at least two isolators per zone, preferably a pair for every 20 to 30 devices; Class B spurs only as tapping from the loop. Check riser and loop diagrams, and that no other service shares the fire alarm cables. Circuit-integrity cable requirements come from NBC (see References, IS 16246).

items.req: The control and indicating equipment is at a control centre (preferably on the ground floor) with a mimic or zone chart; a repeater or annunciator panel is provided near the main entrance where the panel is elsewhere; and every detector has an identification number recorded at the control centre.
items.app: Where a fire alarm system is provided
items.guide: Example ID from Cl. 6.1: Z1/SDI/20 = zone 1, smoke detector (ionisation), 20th detector. Check that panel device text matches the labels on site for a sample. NBC fire command centre requirements are in Section J.

items.req: Where beam, aspirating or duct smoke detectors are used: beam paths are clear and mounted on rigid structure; aspirating air transport time from the farthest sampling point is not more than 120 s with an airflow fault signal; duct detectors are in straight runs at least three duct widths from bends or junctions.
items.app: Atria, warehouses, high spaces and ducts where these detectors are used
items.guide: Beam detectors: no point more than 7.5 m from the beam (8.5 m under pitched roofs); supplementary beams in high spaces such as atria protect a width each side equal to 12.5 percent of beam height; beam coverage must stay within one zone. For aspirating systems, check commissioning records for transport time and the manufacturer's airflow band.

items.req: Routine user tests are carried out and logged: daily panel check; weekly operation of at least one trigger device so that every zone is tested within 13 weeks (a different device each time); weekly visual check of batteries; quarterly inspection with fault simulation, test of alarm and ancillary functions, and a walk-round for changes affecting detector siting.
items.app: Where a fire alarm system is provided
items.guide: Review the log book for the last 3 months: device used in each weekly test, zone rotation, battery remarks and follow-up of defects. The quarterly walk-round (7.4.5(f)) confirms call points unobstructed and conspicuous and a clear space of at least 750 mm radius below detectors (see Ambiguities on 500 mm versus 750 mm). Occupants to be told before tests that sound the alarm (7.4.2).

items.req: At each annual inspection at least 20 percent of detectors are functionally tested so that every detector is tested within 5 years; smoke detector sensitivity is checked by a calibrated method; detectors are cleaned at intervals not exceeding 3 months (or as conditions require); and the electrical installation is tested at least every 3 years.
items.guide: Ask for the detector-wise test matrix showing which detectors were tested each year. Sensitivity cannot be measured with an unmeasured aerosol spray (Note to 7.2.7); spray tests only prove smoke entry. Detectors outside their sensitivity range are replaced (7.2.7.1). After an alarm or fire, exposed detectors are tested as for the annual inspection (7.7).

items.req: Servicing is arranged through a contract with a competent contractor (or a specially trained employee); hospitals, hotels and homes for the elderly have an engineer on call with emergency attendance within 24 h; and replacement detectors are fitted whenever detectors are removed for servicing.
items.app: Where a fire alarm system is provided
items.guide: Check the maintenance contract scope, response-time clause and call-out records. Spares on site: call point covers or glasses, fuses and other essential spares (7.9).

items.req: Fire extinguishers are provided as required by Table 7 and good practice, mounted at a convenient height for quick access.
items.guide: Detailed IS 2190 : 2024 checks are in I-38 to I-45 (selection, distribution, installation, inspection, maintenance, life, register). Check each extinguisher: correct type for the risk, in place, visible, unobstructed, pressure in range, seal and pin intact. Mounting height: the IS 2190 clauses on height are not legible in the copy supplied; see Ambiguities.

items.req: Extinguishers are inspected, tested and refilled by competent persons, with records including hydraulic pressure tests.
items.guide: IS 2190 : 2024 schedule: inspection at about 90 days (8.3), maintenance yearly (8.4), refill and HPT per Annexes E and F; see I-41 to I-43. Check service tags and dates on a sample and the records.

items.req: First-aid hose reels are installed on all floors where required, connected directly to the riser/down-comer main, with hose diameter not less than 19 mm.
items.guide: Run out a sample hose reel fully and open the nozzle: check reach, flow, leaks and that the valve is not seized. IS 3844, Cl. 6.5: no part of the floor more than 6 m from the nozzle with the hose fully run out; annual run-out and flow of at least 30 l/min (Cl. 9.7). See I-47.

items.req: Wet riser, down-comer and yard hydrant systems are provided as required by Table 7, with mains sized as per Table 8.
items.guide: Table 8: 100 mm mains with single outlet landing valves for the buildings and heights listed in its first group; 150 mm for hotels and business buildings above 45 m, starred hotels, institutional above 30 m, industrial above 15 m, storage and hazardous buildings up to 15 m. A dry riser may be used in hilly or industrial areas if the local authority requires (Table 7, Note 24).

items.req: Wet risers are interconnected at terrace level to form a ring, with a cut-off for each connection.
items.app: Where more than one wet riser is provided
items.guide: Inspect at terrace.

items.req: Pressure at the hydraulically remote hydrant and at the highest hydrant is not less than 3.5 bar, and pressure at any hydrant does not exceed 7.0 bar.
items.guide: Witness a flow test at the highest/most remote landing valve with a calibrated gauge. Check lower levels for orifice plates or pressure reducing valves. IS 3844: static pressure in any hose line with the nozzle shut not more than 7 kgf/cm2 (Cl. 7.7); orifice or other device where lower floors exceed 4 kgf/cm2 (Cl. 7.8).

items.req: Hydrants and hose reels are located in the firefighting shaft lobby; hydrants near exit stairs are within 5 m of the exit door; cabinets are marked 'FIRE HOSE CABINET'; and their locations are shown on a floor plan displayed in the stair landing.
items.guide: Cabinet lettering 75 mm high and 12 mm wide, with a glass panel for visibility. IS 3844, Cl. 5.9: landing valve control 1.0 to 1.2 m above floor (see I-46).

items.req: Valves in fixed firefighting installations have supervisory switches signalling to the fire alarm panel, or are chained and padlocked with label and serial-numbered tamper-proof tag, and are kept in the open position.
items.guide: Trace the system from pump to risers and check every isolation valve. Record any closed or partly closed valve as a critical finding.

items.req: External hydrants, internal hydrants, hose reels, hoses, branch pipes and couplings are complete, checked periodically and maintained.
items.guide: Intervals: internal hydrants and hose reels per IS 3844, Cl. 9 (six-monthly inspection, annual hose reel test; see I-50); yard hydrants per IS 13039, Cl. 12 (weekly hydrant and hose box checks, fortnightly mains test; see I-54). Open sample hose boxes: hose, branch pipe and key present; hose condition; landing valve operable; no leaks.

items.req: Static water storage (underground and terrace tanks) of the capacity given in Table 7 is always available, with arrangements for replenishment.
items.guide: Compute actual effective capacity above the top of the pump casing from tank dimensions and compare with Table 7 (add the values in parentheses where basement area exceeds 200 m2, Note 6).

items.req: Fire water is stored in two or more interconnected compartments of equal size.
items.app: Where a static tank is provided
items.guide: Allows cleaning without interrupting water availability.

items.req: Domestic water is drawn only by overflow from the fire tank, or the domestic suction is at a level that always retains the Table 7 fire reserve.
items.app: Where fire and domestic storage are combined
items.guide: Check the suction arrangement on drawings and at site.

items.req: The static tank is accessible to fire engines, has manholes for inspection and suction hose, is not more than 7 m deep from the draw-out level, and the draw-out connection is not more than 5 m from the tank wall.
items.app: Where an underground static tank is provided
items.guide: Check that manhole covers can be opened and are not built over or parked on.

items.req: The tank has a fire brigade collecting head with four 63 mm instantaneous male inlets (two for pumps of 1 400 litre/min) connected by pipe of not less than 150 mm, and a fire brigade draw-out connection.
items.app: Where a static tank is provided
items.guide: Check that inlets are at street level, in a valve box, capped, identified and unobstructed. Draw-out: 63 mm outlet on 100 mm pipe with foot valve.

items.req: Where the tank slab forms part of a driveway, it is designed for a vehicular load of 45 t.
items.guide: Check the structural drawing or designer's certificate.

items.req: Fire water tanks are kept full and free from foreign material; water level is recorded weekly; tanks are cleaned at least once a year.
items.guide: Look into the tank or check the level indicator; review weekly level records and the last cleaning record. IS 15105, Cl. 7.7 allows sprinkler reservoirs to be cleaned once in two years; the NBC annual requirement is stricter and governs.

items.req: Fire pump sets (electric, diesel standby and jockey) of the capacity and number given in Table 7 and its Notes are installed.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Table 7 (cols 13 and 14), Notes 10 to 14, 21 to 23]
items.guide: Notes 10 to 12 and 14 give pump set make-up (main pumps of 1 620, 2 280 or 2 850 litre/min with 180 litre/min jockey pumps). One set per 100 hydrants or part thereof, maximum two sets, interconnected at delivery headers (Note 22). Compare nameplate duty with the requirement. Jockey pump: 3 to 10 percent of installed capacity, minimum 180 l/min (IS 15301, Cl. 6.5); see I-69.

items.req: The pump house is directly accessible from ground level, is not lower than the second basement, and when in a basement has a staircase with direct access from the ground.
items.guide: Installing at ground level is preferable (advisory). Access shall not pass through other occupancies in the basement.

items.req: The pump house is separated by fire walls all around with 120 min fire doors.
items.guide: Check door label and that the door is kept closed. IS 15301, Cl. 4.5 and IS 3844, Cl. 4.2.1 accept a 1 h door; the NBC 120 min requirement governs.

items.req: The pump house is well ventilated, free of water stagnation, large enough for all pumps and accessories, and contains no other utility equipment.
items.guide: 'Well ventilated' is not quantified in NBC. IS 15301, Cl. 4.1 and 4.5 call for natural ventilation through protected windows and forced mechanical ventilation for basement pump rooms; IS 15105, Cl. 9.3.1 limits the rise to 10 deg C above ambient with the diesel engine on full load. Record domestic pumps, stores or other equipment in the room.

items.req: Negative suction arrangements and submersible pumps are not used for fire pumps.
items.guide: Confirm flooded suction: tank low level above the pump casing.

items.req: The diesel engine fire pump battery has a separate charger from the emergency power supply circuit, and the exhaust pipe is insulated and taken to a safe location at ground level.
items.app: Where a diesel fire pump is provided
items.guide: Check battery condition, charger and fuel level. IS 15105, Cl. 9.3.8, 9.3.9: battery capacity for ten consecutive cold starts and a 2-rate trickle charger; see I-67.

items.req: Fire pumps have a soft starter or variable frequency drive starter.
items.app: Where electric fire pumps are provided
items.guide: Check the starter panel.

items.req: Fire pumps are maintained in accordance with good practice, jockey pumps are checked daily, and adequate diesel stock is kept for the design duration.
items.guide: Selector switches shall be found in AUTO. Witness automatic start of jockey, main and diesel pumps by pressure drop (open a test valve). Record cut-in pressures. IS 15301 details are in I-63 to I-69; fuel duration is in I-67 and the Ambiguities sheet.

items.req: Automatic sprinklers are installed throughout the building wherever required by Table 7, in accordance with good practice.
items.guide: Selective sprinklering is a recognised danger (Cl. 5.1.3(b)). Sprinklers may be excluded in substation and DG areas (d) and may be avoided in spaces 17 m or more in height such as atria (e). Record all unsprinklered areas. IS 15105, Cl. 6.2.2: no sprinklers where water discharge is hazardous (e.g. over salt baths, metal melt pans, frying ranges); Cl. 6.2.3: stairs, toilets and switchgear rooms may be left unsprinklered only if separated by 225 mm brick or 100 mm RCC walls with 1 h fire doors.

items.req: Sprinklers are installed in basements where required.
items.guide: Visual check of every basement level, including stores and plant rooms.

items.req: Sprinklers are installed in false ceiling voids exceeding 800 mm in height.
items.guide: Measure void depth at sample locations. IS 15105, Cl. 11.8: roof and ceiling voids more than 0.8 m deep, and floor or ceiling voids that are combustible or contain combustibles, are to be sprinklered.

items.req: Pressure in the sprinkler system does not exceed 12 bar, unless high pressure sprinklers are installed.
items.guide: Read gauges at the lowest level installation control valve.

items.req: The floor area on any one floor protected by one sprinkler riser from an installation control valve does not exceed 4 500 m2.
items.app: Sprinklered buildings (industrial and hazardous: as advised by Authorities)
items.guide: Check against the sprinkler layout.

items.req: Sprinkler installation control valves are inside the fire pump room, and sprinkler flow switches are monitored by the fire alarm panel.
items.guide: Open a floor test/drain valve and confirm the flow signal at the panel and the correct zone.

items.req: Ramps at all levels are protected with sprinklers, and provisions prevent sprinkler/hydrant water entering lifts and electrical rooms.
items.guide: Check sills, slopes or drains at lift lobbies and electrical room doors.

items.req: Sprinklers are fed from both the underground static tank and the terrace tank.
items.app: Where Note 9 applies to the Table 7 row
items.guide: Check piping schematic.

items.req: Sprinkler heads are unobstructed, undamaged, free of paint and corrosion, and of the correct temperature rating; spare heads are kept.
items.guide: Clear space of 0.5 m below deflectors (1 m for high-piled combustible storage and above open-cell ceilings) (11.3). Sprinklers are not painted except for identification, coated, altered, reconditioned or repaired; used or damaged heads are replaced with new ones (15.1.2, 15.1.3). Temperature rating at least 30 deg C above the highest expected ambient (15.5.1.1); bulb colours 57 orange, 68 red, 79 yellow, 93 green, 141 blue, 182 mauve (Table 37). Metal guards where heads may be struck (15.6.1). Record storage stacked close to heads, heads blocked by partitions, ducts or signage, and painted, corroded or missing heads. Spare stock: see I-60.

items.req: Automatic high velocity water spray or emulsifying systems protect oil-cooled transformers, and medium velocity water spray protects cable galleries and similar risks, where applicable.
items.guide: Check deluge valve, detection, nozzle condition and test records.

items.req: A fixed foam system protects the boiler oil storage area and ancillary furnace oil storage in the basement.
items.app: Where oil storage for boilers is in the basement
items.guide: Check foam concentrate quantity, expiry and test records.

items.req: Gas based or clean agent suppression is provided where water or foam cannot be used, in accordance with good practice.
items.app: Server rooms, control rooms and similar special risks
items.guide: Check cylinder pressure/weight, room integrity (sealed openings, door closers), abort/manual release, warning signs and service records.

items.req: Fixed firefighting installations are maintained in accordance with good practice and Part 12, and commissioning test records are available.
items.guide: Review the maintenance contract scope, service reports for the last 12 months and open defects. Commissioning benchmarks: internal hydrant system held at 7 kgf/cm2 for 30 min with a drop of not more than 0.5 kgf/cm2, then a flow test (IS 3844, 8.1, 8.2); sprinkler and hydrant pipework held at 150 percent of maximum working pressure for 2 h (IS 15105, 10.1.6; IS 13039, 7.6); each sprinkler installation valve tested with automatic pump start (IS 15105, 18.3).

items.req: Fire extinguishers are ISI-marked and of types suited to the classes of fire present: Class A for building protection; Class B / C where flammable liquids or gases are present; Class F for cooking oils and fats; Class D for combustible metals; and types tested and marked for energized electrical equipment.
items.guide: IS 2190 : 2024 applies only to ISI-marked extinguishers to IS 15683 and IS 16018 (Foreword). Energized electrical equipment: CO2, powder, clean agent or water-mist types marked as suitable; CO2 with metal horns is not safe on live equipment (6.3.7). Clean agent types only where a clean medium is needed (6.2). AFFF / FFFP not for water-soluble (polar) liquids unless the nameplate says so (6.4.3). Extinguishers in one building should operate alike (Foreword). Fire buckets do not count in lieu of extinguishers.

items.req: Extinguishers are distributed per the hazard: Class A rating, travel distance and area per extinguisher as Table 1 (light 2A, 20 m, 300 m2; moderate 3A, 20 m, 150 m2; high 4A, 15 m, 100 m2); Class B / C as Table 2 (55B, 144B, 233B; 15 m); and at least two per floor (one where the floor is under 100 m2).
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Table 7 (col 3); IS 2190 : 2024, Cl. 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, Tables 1 and 2]
