items.guide: Classify each area as light, moderate or high hazard (Cl. 3.6; Annex B, Table 6 gives example criteria, e.g. building over 15 m or more than 250 occupants = high). Measure walking distance, not straight line. Other limits: Class B liquids in depth over 6 mm per 7.4 (travel not more than 15 m); Class D within 20 m (7.6.2); Class F within 10 m, sized by cooking area per Table 3 (7.7, see L-23). Two adjacent 2A water extinguishers may count as one 3A or 4A (Table 1 footnote).

items.req: Extinguishers are kept in their designated places, conspicuous and unobstructed along normal paths of travel, with location signs where not directly visible, mounted on hangers, brackets or in unlocked cabinets, and not exposed to temperatures outside the range marked on them.
items.guide: Floor stands only where wall mounting is not possible (5.5). Locked cabinets only where vandalism occurs, with means of emergency access (5.3). Outdoor or hot-location cabinets need ventilation openings, a drain and insect mesh (5.10). Service and HPT labels must not obscure operating instructions. Mounting height: NBC says 'convenient height'; the IS 2190 clauses on mounting height and impact protection are not legible in the copy supplied, so confirm from the printed standard (see Ambiguities).

items.req: Every extinguisher is inspected when placed in service and at about 90-day intervals: in its place, unobstructed, instructions legible and facing out, seals and tamper indicators intact, full (weighed or hefted), no damage, corrosion, leakage or blocked nozzle, gauge in the operable range, bracket secure, tags intact; and deficiencies are corrected at once.
items.guide: The 90-day interval is worded 'should'; the check points are 'shall'. The 2024 revision dropped the monthly inspection (Foreword). Check a sample on site against these points and the last quarterly record. Non-rechargeable units with damage, low pressure or broken seals are removed from service (8.3.5, 8.3.6).

items.req: All extinguishers receive maintenance once a year (not less than six months apart) by competent persons; each carries a tag showing the month and year of service and the person who did it; and units removed for service are replaced at once by spares of the same type and at least equal rating.
items.guide: Competent person (Annex C): at least 3 months practical experience plus a course of at least 32 h with an examination supervised by an independent body, and a 4 h refresher every 5 years; ask for certificates. Service labels not on the front of the extinguisher (10.4); unique ID number per extinguisher (10.5); gauges replaced or calibrated at HPT (10.6); rupture disc replaced at each HPT or every 5 years (10.7).

items.req: Extinguishers are discharged and refilled, and hydrostatically pressure tested, at the intervals in Annexes E and F: water, foam and cartridge-type powder refilled every 3 years; stored-pressure powder, CO2 and clean agent every 5 years; HPT every 3 years for water and foam and every 5 years for powder, CO2 and clean agent; CO2 cylinders pressure tested before every refill.
items.guide: HPT test pressures (Annex F): 35 kg/cm2 for water, foam, powder and clean agent (held 150 s); 225 kg/cm2 for CO2 (held 30 s). Check HPT dates on a sample against the date of manufacture. Corrosive environments: discharge tests at half the interval are desirable (Annex E, Note 1). Condemn units that fail HPT or show weld or solder repairs, pitting, damaged threads, fire exposure or dents beyond the limits of 11.1.3.

items.req: No extinguisher is beyond its service life from date of manufacture (10 years for water, foam, powder and clean agent; 15 years for CO2), and obsolete types (soda-acid, chemical foam, inverting, CTC or CBM, copper or brass shells joined by soft solder or rivets, and non-rechargeable units more than 5 years old) have been removed.
items.guide: Read the year of manufacture on a sample. Rejected extinguishers are to be cut across the body before disposal and the rejection and disposal recorded in the register (Cl. 13).

items.req: A register of fire extinguishers is kept in the Annex H format, recording for each unit: type, capacity, year of manufacture, make, location, quarterly and annual inspection dates, pressure test date, discharge date, refill date and next due date.
items.guide: Cross-check three units picked on site against the register.

items.req: Internal hydrant landing valves are provided on every floor (and on an accessible roof) in the staircase lobby or enclosure without reducing the escape width, with the outlet 1.0 to 1.2 m above floor, housed in glass-fronted hose boxes with hose and branch pipe, and with clearance to connect and operate the hose.
items.guide: Each single-headed hydrant: not less than 30 m of 63 mm hose (IS 636, Type A) in two 15 m lengths with couplings, and a branch pipe (5.12). Hose box of at least 2 mm MS plate with glass front, sized for the valve, hoses and branch pipes (5.14). Basements are to be covered by hydrants and hose reels (5.10). Note: IS 3844 Tables 1 and 2 (system type by building) are superseded by NBC Tables 7 and 8.

items.req: Hose reels are sited on each floor near exits, staircases or lobbies so that, with the hose fully run out, no part of the floor is more than 6 m from the nozzle; they are unobstructed, firmly fixed, and preferably recessed out of the escape route.
items.guide: Walk the hose to the farthest corner of sampled rooms. Recess doors should open about 180 degrees; in open areas the inlet valve and nozzle retainer about 900 mm above floor (6.2). In warehouses, keep stacks away from hose reels, using guard rails if needed (6.4). Hose reel to IS 884, Type A (IS 884 not in project files).

items.req: Each wet riser (or riser zone) has a fire service inlet at ground level on the street side, preferably near the main entrance, fitted with a non-return valve, in a lockable glass-fronted box marked 'FIRE SERVICE INLET', with 2 x 63 mm inlets for a 100 mm main or 4 x 63 mm for a 150 mm main; and each main has an air release valve at the top and a drain.
items.guide: One inlet may serve two risers within 30 m of each other (5.5.1(a)). Box: 1.6 mm MS plate, 4 mm glass front; lettering at least 75 mm high and 12 mm wide in fluorescent fire red. Check that a fire tender can reach the inlet, that it is not blocked by parking or landscaping, and that caps are present. Inlets are to be inspected every six months (9.3).

items.req: Spare hoses and accessories are kept ready: at least 10 percent of hoses, landing valves, lugs and valve wheels for internal hydrants; for yard hydrants spare hose of 10 percent (minimum 30 m) and spare nozzles of 10 percent (minimum two); and spare rubber washers packed in French chalk.
items.guide: IS 3844 uses 'should' for internal hydrant spares; IS 13039 uses 'shall' for yard hydrants. Spare hose in 15 m lengths with couplings attached.

items.req: Internal hydrant and hose reel systems are maintained: surroundings and indicator plates checked; isolating valves locked open; inlets, landing valves, drain valves and box hinges and locks inspected every six months; hose reels fully run out and flow tested at least once a year (not less than 30 l/min; at least the highest reel on each riser); defects rectified promptly.
items.app: Where internal hydrants or hose reels are provided
items.guide: Review the six-monthly and annual records. A defective landing valve without a replacement should be removed and the outlet blanked so the riser stays live (9.4). The annual hose reel test also proves couplings watertight (9.7).

items.req: Yard (external) hydrants are stand-post type with oblique 63 mm instantaneous outlets about 1 m above ground, serially numbered, easily accessible with no storage around them, guarded where vehicles may hit them, and located at least 2 m from, and within 15 m of, the building face they protect.
items.app: Where yard hydrants are provided (IS 13039 covers medium and large industrial risks; apply as good practice elsewhere)
items.guide: Spacing (4.12): at least one hydrant per 60 m of external wall for light hazard, 45 m for ordinary and 30 m for high hazard. High-hazard buildings: hydrants 5 to 15 m from the building face (4.16). Remote hydrants need paved approach paths (4.8). Underground hydrants only in surface boxes 750 mm square (4.1). Pressure-reducing devices where pressure exceeds 7 kg/cm2 (4.6). No connection for any other purpose from the hydrant service (4.3).

items.req: Hose and branch pipes for yard hydrants are kept either in glass-fronted hose boxes beside each hydrant (two 15 m lengths of 63 mm hose each) or in central hose stations, shaded from the sun, with a master key for locked boxes kept at the main gate or another known location.
items.guide: Central hose stations: two 15 m lengths for each of the first ten hydrants plus one per additional hydrant, reducible above 55 outlets (8.2.1). Nozzles: half the number of hose lengths, 16 to 25 mm bore (32 mm for high hazard) (8.4, 9.1). Hose lengths marked and numbered (8.7, recommended).

items.req: Hydrant mains are laid as a ring (terminal mains only where a ring is not feasible), buried at least 1 m deep or carried above ground on masonry or RCC supports, not under buildings, with sectional isolation valves in marked surface boxes so that any section can be isolated without affecting the rest.
items.app: Where yard hydrant mains are provided
items.guide: Isolation valves near loop junctions and at least every 300 m (7.15.1); right-hand valves with open/close arrows; surface box at least 1 m2 with a fire-red plate giving valve number and direction (7.16). Above-ground mains at least 6 m (15 m for high hazard) from buildings and storage, supported at not more than 6 m (3 m below 150 mm), not on pipe racks (7.3). Terminal mains: 80 mm feeds 1 hydrant, 100 mm 2, 125 mm 3, 150 mm 5 (7.13). Butterfly valves above 150 mm gear operated (7.15.5).

items.req: External hydrant systems are maintained to the IS 13039 schedule: hydrants examined weekly; hose boxes inspected weekly and cleaned monthly; mains tested fortnightly with a pump at maximum pressure and two 30 m hose lines running; cut-off valves operated monthly and overhauled annually; a hose register kept.
items.guide: Hose cut back to less than 90 percent of its original length, or unserviceable for any reason, is discarded (12.4.2, 12.4.4). Fire hose not used for any purpose other than fire protection and drills (12.4.5). Spare washers for hydrant valve seats (12.3.2).

items.req: When any part of a hydrant or sprinkler system is out of service, only the affected section is isolated (blank flanges rather than valves left shut overnight), only one tank compartment is emptied at a time, compensatory measures are applied, the fire service and occupants are informed, and a notice is displayed.
items.guide: Compensatory measures (IS 15105, 17.2.2): close fire doors and shutters, alert security and safety staff, add first-aid appliances. Patrol the area before shut-down (17.3.2); notify department heads in writing (17.3.3); keep authorities informed (17.3.1). If a pump is expected to be down for more than 72 h, connect an alternative supply (IS 13039, 13.3). Ask for the impairment or shut-down log for the last 12 months.

items.req: Sprinkler spacing and coverage match the hazard class: light hazard not more than 21 m2 per sprinkler (17 m2 sidewall) and 4.5 m spacing; moderate hazard not more than 12 m2 (9 m2 sidewall) and 4.0 m spacing (4.6 m along ranges if staggered); high hazard not more than 9 m2 and 3.7 m spacing; not less than 2 m between sprinklers; distance to walls not more than half the spacing.
items.guide: Confirm the hazard class used in design (Cl. 5.1): offices, hotels, hospitals and schools are light hazard only where rooms are 125 m2 or less and bounded by masonry walls with doors, otherwise moderate; car parks and retail stores are moderate. Distance to boundary not more than 1.5 m where walls are combustible or joists and rafters are exposed. Sidewall and staggered layouts are not permitted in high hazard (11.2.3.5). Measure spacing at sample locations and compare with the layout drawing.

items.req: Sprinkler deflectors are correctly positioned (75 to 150 mm below non-combustible ceilings; sidewall heads 100 to 150 mm below the ceiling and 50 to 150 mm from the wall), clear of beams as Table 13, and additional sprinklers are fitted below ducts, platforms and other obstructions more than 1 m wide (more than 0.8 m wide where within 150 mm of a wall).
items.guide: Beams or joists deeper than 300 mm (combustible ceiling) or 450 mm (non-combustible) form separate bays (11.4.1.3). A sprinkler within 0.6 m of a column needs another within 2 m on the opposite side (11.5). Check under ducts and cable trays added after commissioning, and below mezzanines, platforms and worktables with a power source. Ceiling voids: see I-27.

items.req: In storage areas goods are kept at least 1.5 m below sprinkler deflectors where possible (2 m for jute), aisles are at least 2.5 m and stacks not more than 150 m2, storage heights are within the limits of the design category, and intermediate rack sprinklers are provided where storage exceeds those limits.
items.app: Storage occupancies and storage areas within other buildings
items.guide: Compare actual goods category (I to IV, Cl. 5.1.4) and stack height with the design basis. Moderate-hazard storage limits (Table 4): 4.0 m (Cat I), 3.0 m (II), 2.0 m (III), 1.25 m (IV); above these the risk becomes high-hazard storage needing a higher design density. Exceeding the aisle or stack limits adds 2.5 l/min/m2 to the design density (8.1.5.4). Intermediate sprinklers: vertical spacing not more than 3 m, 150 mm clear above goods, metal guards and water shields (11.13, 15.6).

items.req: Each installation control valve set has the main stop valve secured open by a padlocked or riveted strap and readily accessible, a 'SPRINKLER STOP VALVE' location plate and a plan of the risk showing valve positions, 'B' and 'C' pressure gauges, a numbered alarm valve matching its numbered water motor gong on an external wall, and test and drain valves.
items.guide: Where one risk is served by several alarm valves, the area served by each is displayed near the valves (14.7.6.3). Valves right-handed with an open/shut indicator (14.1.2). Gauge scale subdivisions not coarser than 0.2 bar up to 10 bar (14.10.1). Water motor gong not more than 6 m above the alarm valve connection, with a strainer (14.9.2). NBC requires the control valves inside the pump room (I-30); the location plate and plan still apply.

items.req: A stock of spare sprinklers of each type and temperature rating, with sprinkler spanners, is kept on the premises at not more than 38 deg C: 6 / 24 / 36 for light / moderate / high hazard (in or within 100 km of a state capital), or 25 / 50 / 100 elsewhere.
items.guide: Increase in proportion where there is more than one installation. Check that the spares match the installed types (upright, pendent, concealed, sidewall) and ratings.

items.req: Water storage reserved for sprinklers is not less than Table 2 of IS 15105 (light: 20 min pumping or 35 m3; moderate: 1 h or 200 m3; high: 2 h), is in two interconnected compartments where 225 m3 or more, has a level indicator, and where combined with other systems holds the total of all systems served.
items.app: Sprinklered premises where NBC Table 7 does not fix the storage (for example industrial and storage buildings); NBC Table 7 governs where it applies
items.guide: Combined reservoirs are acceptable only where all suction inlets are at the same level (7.4). Level indicator preferably graduated in m3 (7.6). Salt or brackish water is not normally allowed (7.3).

items.req: Sprinkler installations are inspected and tested to the IS 15105 schedule: gauge readings above and below each installation valve recorded daily and weekly; alarm gong operated weekly with the time to sound recorded; installation valves serviced annually; discharge (inspector's) test at least every six months; system flushed; pressure gauges calibrated annually.
items.guide: The user keeps a log book available on demand (17.1). Gong audibility at least 85 dB above background (18.6.2); gong assembly checked every 3 months (17.6.5.3). The text and Table 38 differ on flushing and flow test intervals (see Ambiguities). After any operation, operated heads and heat-affected heads nearby are replaced with new ones (17.5, 15.1.2).

items.req: Each fire pump has a pressure gauge between the pump and its non-return valve, a nameplate giving rated head, capacity and speed, an independent suction, a test line with shut-off valve for testing without discharging into the system, and a circulation relief valve set below shut-off pressure.
items.guide: No sluice or cut-off valve on the suction unless the pump is below the water level (6.8). Suction velocity not more than 1.5 m/s, or 2 m/s with flooded suction (6.9). Delivery: sluice valve upstream of the non-return valve; no butterfly valves inside the pump room on hydrant services (IS 13039, 5.1.10). Relief valve discharge about 3 to 5 percent of pump rating (6.11).

items.req: The pump room gives working clearance around pumps (1 m front and back and 0.75 m at sides and between pumps above 2 280 l/min; 0.75 m and 0.6 m for smaller pumps; 2.75 m headroom), has a floor sloped to a drain, normal and emergency lighting, a lifting girder, a CO2 or DCP extinguisher, and a displayed layout of pumps and fire water lines.
items.guide: Basement pump rooms are desirable to be sprinklered (6.16) and need forced mechanical ventilation (4.5). IS 15301 accepts a 1 h door for a pump house inside the building; the NBC 120 min requirement governs (I-19).

items.req: Pumps start automatically on pressure drop through separate pressure switches (jockey: cut-in and cut-out; main and diesel: cut-in only), main pumps stop only by a manual push button, electric and diesel pumps are interlocked so that both do not run together, and pump starting sounds an audible alarm outside the pump house.
items.guide: Record cut-in pressures of jockey, main and diesel pumps and confirm they are staggered so the jockey handles small losses and the main pumps start in sequence. Diesel panel with its own battery, charger and auto/manual changeover (5.3); air vessel with pressure switches on the delivery line (5.4). Audible pump-run alarm outside the pump house, and at the site fire station if any, is 'shall' in IS 13039. After a fire, pump stopping is manual only (IS 15105, 17.5.3). NBC also requires pump status at the fire alarm panel (H-08).

items.req: The fire pump supply is independent of all other loads (taken from the incoming side of the main LT breaker, or from the busbars), protected by a breaker without under-voltage release and set to allow emergency overload, fed by a dedicated armoured feeder not passing under buildings, with tell-tale lamps in the substation and pump room and spare fuses in a glass-fronted box in the pump house.
items.app: Where electric fire pumps are provided
items.guide: Verify on the single line diagram and at the main LT panel that switching off the building supply does not isolate the fire pumps. With two sources, changeover should not need manual switching (IS 15105, 9.2.8). Substation or DG set supplying the pumps 6 m from other buildings or separated by a 4 h wall (IS 15301, 6.13).

items.req: The diesel fire pump engine accepts full load within 15 s of the start signal, has battery capacity for ten consecutive cold starts with a 2-rate trickle charger, a gravity-feed fuel tank with level gauge and the fuel valve locked open, an hour counter, and fuel stored for the required running time.
items.app: Where a diesel fire pump is provided
items.guide: Fuel duration differs between standards: IS 15105 tank for 1 / 2 / 3 h full load (light / moderate / high hazard) plus 3 h on hand; IS 13039 tank for 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 h (light / ordinary / high A / high B) plus 6 h on hand; IS 15301 at least 4 h. See Ambiguities. Separate tank and feed pipe for each engine; no soldered joints or plastic tubing. Engine room at not less than 4.5 deg C (IS 15105, 9.3.13), heated above 10 deg C in sub-zero conditions. Spare parts and tool kit on hand (filters, belts, injector nozzles, gaskets).

items.req: Fire pumps are tested and maintained to a written schedule, recorded in a register kept in the pump house: jockey pump tested daily by pressure drop; main pumps run at least 5 minutes daily; diesel engine started on pressure drop and run regularly; weekly checks of glands, bearings, starter contacts, fuel and batteries; annual flow test.
items.guide: Diesel running: weekly for 10 min per IS 15301; 5 min daily per IS 15105 and IS 13039 (see Ambiguities). Insulation resistance: weekly per IS 15301, six-monthly per IS 15105 and IS 13039. A responsible person in charge of pump maintenance (IS 15301, 7.1); trained pump operator on all shifts (IS 13039, 12.1.1.1; IS 15105, 17.6.1.5). The register should start with the commissioning test (flow at 7 kgf/cm2, flow at 4.5 kgf/cm2, and shut-off pressure not more than 120 percent of 7 kgf/cm2) for comparison with later tests (IS 15301, 7.2.1).

items.req: Main fire pumps deliver at least 150 percent of rated capacity at not less than 65 percent of rated head, with shut-off head not more than 120 percent of rated head (140 percent for vertical turbine pumps), and the jockey pump capacity is between 3 percent (minimum 180 l/min) and 10 percent of the installed pumping capacity.
items.guide: Obtain pump curves and the latest flow test. IS 13039 limits the jockey to 3 to 5 percent (minimum 10.8 m3/h) on hydrant services (see Ambiguities). Motor rated for the power at 150 percent of rated discharge (IS 15105, 9.2.10); diesel engine rated for the higher of 120 percent of duty-point power and the power at 150 percent flow (9.3.2.3).

items.req: A fire command centre is provided on the entrance floor with direct access, housing the main fire alarm panel and public address communication to all floors.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Cl. 3.4.12(a); Annex D, Cl. D-6]
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) and other buildings where required
items.guide: Check that the route from the fire tender arrival point to the room is direct and signed.

items.req: The fire command centre has 120 min rated walls, a fire door and emergency lighting, and interior finishes are not flammable.
items.app: Where a fire command centre is provided
items.guide: Visual check; door label.

items.req: All controls and monitoring of fire alarm, pressurization and smoke management systems are in the fire command centre.
items.app: Where a fire command centre is provided
items.guide: BMS, CCTV and other critical monitoring may also be here (advisory).

items.req: Two laminated and bound sets of all floor plans with details of firefighting equipment and installations are kept in the fire command centre.
items.app: Where a fire command centre is provided
items.guide: Check that plans reflect the current layout.

items.req: The fire command centre is staffed, and the staff in charge maintain the services and firefighting equipment in coordination with security, electrical and civil staff.
items.app: Where a fire command centre is provided
items.guide: Check the 24-hour roster and operator competence (ask the operator to identify an alarm location and make a PA announcement).

items.req: The fire command station has adequate illumination, communication to mechanical equipment rooms and lift control rooms, a copy of the Fire Safety Plan, the Building Information Form and representative floor plans.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex D, Cl. D-8.10, D-9.8, D-9.9]
items.app: High rise (15 m and above) (Annex D guidelines)
items.guide: Check documents are present and current.

items.req: A firefighting shaft is provided for each residential building/tower, each educational building/block, and each compartment of institutional, assembly, business and mercantile occupancies.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex E, Cl. E-2; Cl. 2.24]
items.guide: For other occupancies the requirement is settled with the local fire authority. The shaft has 120 min protection and connects directly to exit discharge or through a 120 min exit passageway.

items.req: The firefighting shaft has a protected lobby, staircase and fireman's lift, 120 min fire doors, firemen talk-back, and a wet riser with landing valve in its lobby.
items.guide: The lobby of an enclosed shaft should display the floor plan (Note 2 to Fig. 2, recommendation). Smoke control of the staircase and lift lobby follows Cl. 4.4.2.5 and Table 6.

items.req: At least one fireman's lift is provided per building, per wing and per bank of lifts, identified on the building plan displayed in the fire command centre.
items.guide: Confirm identification on plans and at landings.

items.req: The fireman's lift has a floor area of minimum 1.43 m2, loading capacity not less than 544 kg (8 persons), power operated doors of minimum 0.8 m width, and speed sufficient to reach the top floor from the fire access level within 1 min.
items.guide: Check nameplate; time a run from access level to the top served landing.

items.req: The fireman's lift has a two-position fireman's switch in a glass-fronted box at the evacuation floor, and operates correctly in Phase I (return to evacuation floor) and Phase II (car control only).
items.guide: Witness the test with the lift maintainer: on switch ON, landing calls are cancelled, the car returns non-stop to the evacuation floor and parks with doors open; in Phase II it responds to car calls only.

items.req: All lifts have Phase I grounding operation, initiated by switch or by signal from the fire alarm system.
items.guide: Witness grounding of all lifts on a simulated alarm.

items.req: The fireman's lift has a reliable alternative power source with changeover, fire-safe wiring route, the words 'Fireman Lift' in fluorescent paint at the landing, and arrangements to keep firefighting water out of the lift shaft.
items.guide: The alternative supply is a 'should' in the clause, but Part 4 Cl. 3.4.6.2 makes emergency power to fireman's lifts mandatory.

items.req: Lift well enclosures have a fire rating of 120 min with a vent at the top of not less than 0.2 m2 per lift, and landing doors are imperforate with minimum 60 min fire resistance.
items.guide: Collapsible landing and car doors are not permitted.

items.req: Communication facilities are provided in the lift car and lift main lobby and are connected to the fire control room.
items.guide: Test the intercom from a car.

items.req: Refuge areas are provided and sized for the occupants of two consecutive floors at 0.3 m2 per person, plus one wheelchair space of 0.9 m2 for every 200 occupants or part thereof, with a minimum of 15 m2.
items.guide: High rise apartment buildings with balconies need not have refuge areas up to 60 m; above 60 m, at 60 m and every 30 m thereafter. For D-6, Cl. 6.4.2.2 governs. Compute required area from the occupant load and measure the area provided.

items.req: Refuge areas are on the periphery of the floor, open to air on at least one side with railings, located at or immediately above 24 m and thereafter at every 15 m.
items.guide: The clause says 'every 15 m or so'; use 15 m as the benchmark.

items.req: Refuge areas are always kept clear, with no storage of combustible materials or electrical and mechanical equipment.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex E, Cl. E-4(j); NBC 2016, Part 12, Cl. 15.15]
items.guide: Inspect every refuge area. Record enclosures, conversion to other use, storage and locked access.

items.req: Each refuge area is ventilated, sprinklered, and provided with first aid box, fire extinguishers, public address speaker, fireman talk-back, emergency lighting, drinking water and drainage.
items.guide: Check each item on site.

items.req: A 'REFUGE AREA' sign with letters of minimum 75 mm, also showing locations of refuge areas on floors above and below, is installed at the entry and within the refuge area.
items.guide: Measure letter height.

items.req: Refuge areas are approachable by an accessible means of egress and connect to the firefighting shaft without occupants having to return through the spaces they came from.
items.guide: Walk the route from the floor to the refuge area and on to the shaft.

items.req: Horizontal exits are through 120 min fire doors in fire resistant walls, openable at all times from both sides, swinging in the direction of exit travel.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex E, Cl. E-4(a) to (c), (n)]
items.guide: Level differences are ramped at not steeper than 1 in 12.

items.req: Sprinklers are fed from the main riser and an alternate/standby riser with isolation valves.
items.app: Residential above 120 m; other occupancies above 60 m
items.guide: Check the riser schematic.

items.req: Fire water storage and pumps are provided at intermediate levels, with a fire pump room connected to the firefighting shaft.
items.guide: Tanks at 160 m to 180 m and at intermediate floors above, each at least half of the Table 7 underground capacity, with one working and one standby pump of 2 850 litre/min.

items.req: Seismic bracing of firefighting installations is considered.
items.guide: The clause says bracing 'shall be considered' depending on seismic vulnerability and occupancy; treat as advisory unless the design basis commits to it.

items.req: A helipad is provided.
items.guide: Recommendation only.

items.req: Gas pipes run in separate shafts used exclusively for the purpose, on external walls and away from staircases; distribution pipes are below the false ceiling.
items.app: Where piped gas / LPG reticulation is installed
items.guide: Trace the route from the bank or meter to the points of use.

items.req: Gas lines are not installed through electrical shafts, escape routes or refuge areas.
items.guide: Visual check.

items.req: Kitchens working on LPG are not located in basements.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Cl. 4.7.9; Annex G, Cl. G-3(f)]
items.guide: Check all basement levels, including staff canteens and pantries.

items.req: Gas cylinders and manifolds are housed in a detached, ventilated enclosure at the distances prescribed in good practice, away from air intakes, smoke exhaust openings and windows.
items.app: Where LPG cylinders / manifolds are used
items.guide: Separation distances come from IS 6044, which is not in the project files. Medium velocity spray nozzles for the enclosure are desirable (advisory).

items.req: The building has an approved outside gas shut-off valve, conspicuously marked.
items.guide: Check it is accessible and that staff know its location.

items.req: Pressure regulating stations with excess flow shut-off valves are installed, and a seismic shut-off valve is provided at the main distribution point.
items.app: Gas installations (seismic valve: D-6 and institutional above 15 m)
items.guide: Check installation and test records.

items.req: Gas leak detectors are provided at usage points and monitored from the fire command centre, with circuit integrity signal cables.
items.guide: Test a detector with the maintainer.

items.req: Gas meters are housed in a metal cupboard in a well-ventilated space.
items.guide: Ventilation position should suit the gas: LPG is heavier than air, town gas lighter.

items.req: Thermal detectors are installed in the fume hoods of large kitchens, with automatic tripping of the exhaust fan and shut-off of gas in case of fire.
items.app: Large kitchens of hotels, hospitals and similar in high rise buildings
items.guide: The gas valve is hand re-set type, accessible and segregated from cooking ranges.

items.req: Commercial kitchens are separated from other parts of the building by compartment walls and floors of at least 60 min, with 60 min self-closing doors to food serving areas.
items.app: Commercial kitchens in centrally air conditioned buildings (Annex G scope)
items.guide: Open kitchens need 60 min fire rated glass or drop fire curtains (G-3(c)).

items.req: In a building that is not sprinkler protected, the commercial kitchen floor area does not exceed 50 m2.
items.guide: Measure.

items.req: An automatic fixed fire suppression system protects all cooking equipment producing grease laden vapours, the hoods, grease removal devices and exhaust ducts.
items.guide: Wet chemical or equivalent approved system for hoods; no sprinklers within 3 m of cooking equipment and hoods (G-5.2(b)). Check nozzles, caps, cylinder pressure, fusible links/detectors and service tags.

items.req: On actuation of the kitchen suppression system, power and gas to the equipment are cut off automatically, the supply fan stops, the exhaust fan keeps running, an alarm sounds and the fire alarm system is signalled; a manual actuating device is in the means of egress.
items.guide: Review the last functional test report; witness a simulated test where possible.

items.req: Gas leakage detectors are provided in all kitchens, linked to a gas solenoid valve for emergency shut-off and integrated with the fire alarm system.
items.app: Commercial kitchens using gas (Annex G scope)
items.guide: Test with the maintainer.

items.req: Kitchen exhaust ducts are cleaned every six months, and grease filters are accessible, removable and cleaned.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex G, Cl. G-5.3(c), G-5.4(k)]
items.guide: Ask for duct cleaning records with before/after photographs; inspect a duct access panel for grease build-up.

items.req: Fire extinguishers near cooking areas and hoods are suitable for the type of fire.
items.guide: Suitability by class of fire comes from IS 2190 (not in project files).

items.req: Equipment using dry fuel (wood/charcoal) has independent exhaust ducts or approved spark arrestors.
items.guide: Check spark arrestors are accessible and cleaned.

items.req: Kitchen exhaust terminates with at least 3 m horizontal clearance to adjacent buildings, property lines and air intakes, and 1.5 m to any combustible structure.
items.guide: Measure at the termination.

items.req: Boilers and boiler rooms conform to The Boilers Act, 1923.
items.guide: Check the boiler inspection certificate and its validity. The Act is not in the project files.

items.req: Boilers are in a 180 min fire resisting room with a 120 min door, dedicated ventilation not routed through electrical rooms or exits, and a dyked oil tank (10 percent extra volume, sand filled to 300 mm).
items.guide: The clause introduces these as aspects that 'may be taken into account'.

items.req: Rooms containing high pressure boilers, refrigerating machinery, transformers or other equipment subject to possible explosion are not directly under or adjacent to exits, are cut off from the rest of the building and vented to outside air.
items.guide: All high hazard rooms or areas shall be segregated or protected by 120 min fire resistant walls.

items.req: Flammable liquids, gases and other hazardous materials are identified, kept to the minimum needed, and stored in designated, ventilated, segregated locations.
items.ref: [Good practice; see NBC 2016, Part 4, Cl. 4.8 and Annex D, Cl. D-9.8(w)]
items.guide: NBC requires segregation of high hazard areas (Cl. 4.8) and listing in the building information form. Quantities and licensing fall under the Petroleum Act and other rules not in the project files. Record paint, solvent, diesel, LPG and chemical stores.

items.req: Commercial kitchens have Class F rated extinguishers within 10 m travel of cooking appliances, sized by cooking area per Table 3 of IS 2190 (5F per 0.03 m2, 15F per 0.05 m2, 25F per 0.08 m2, 75F per 0.25 m2 of cooking area).
items.app: Kitchens using cooking oils or fats
items.guide: Check the Class F rating marked on the label; ABC powder or CO2 is not a substitute for a Class F rating. Hood suppression systems, where fitted, are additional.

items.req: Parking structures within, above, below, attached to or less than 3 m from a building used for another purpose are separated by walls and floors of not less than 120 min fire resistance.
items.guide: Incidental cashier/attendant booths and toilets up to 200 m2 in total are excluded.

items.req: Vehicle ramps are not counted as exits unless pedestrian facilities are provided, and means of egress from parking meet Clause 4.
items.guide: Check stair access from every parking level and travel distance.

items.req: No fuel dispensing is carried out in the building, and any car repair facility is separated by 120 min fire resistant construction.
items.guide: Look for informal repair, washing with solvents and fuel storage in parking areas.

items.req: Sprinklers in car parking are standard response type with minimum K-factor of 80 and area coverage of 9 m2.
items.guide: IS 15105 classes car parking within buildings or basements as moderate hazard: design density 5 l/min/m2 over 360 m2 (8.1.2), not more than 12 m2 per sprinkler and 4.0 m spacing (11.2.2). Check head markings (15 mm, K-80), spacing, and obstruction by ducts and cable trays.

items.req: Basement car parking is compartmented (3 000 m2 when sprinklered) by fire barriers, water curtain or a combination.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex H, Cl. H-4(c) to (e); Cl. 4.5.2]
items.guide: Water curtain: deluge system operated by sprinkler flow switch, fed by an independent electric pump, with water for 60 min for the largest compartment perimeter in addition to existing storage.

items.req: All fire exit doors from car parking to exits are painted green and display exit signage.
items.guide: Visual check.

items.req: Stilt parking is sprinklered where the building is required to be sprinklered, and open-to-sky car parking in a complex with a hydrant system is covered by yard hydrants.
items.guide: Visual check. Yard hydrant details per IS 13039 are in I-51 to I-54.

items.req: Hydraulic oil tanks and pumps for car lifts located below ground have appropriate fire detection and suppression.
items.guide: Visual check.

items.req: Parking floors are non-combustible and slope towards drains.
items.guide: Check for standing water and oil.

items.req: The atrium is in a building of Type 1 or Type 2 construction, and combustible furnishings and decorations on the atrium floor are limited and sparsely distributed.
items.guide: 'Limited and sparsely distributed' is not quantified; see the Ambiguities sheet. Record kiosks, exhibitions, vehicles on display and seasonal decorations.

items.req: Smoke detectors are provided on the underside of each floor protruding into the atrium, at the atrium roof and adjacent to each return air intake; beam or aspirating detectors are used within the atrium space.
items.guide: Check device types and test records.

items.req: Sprinklers at 450 mm to 600 mm from the glass protect glazed areas of retail, tenant and other areas adjoining the exit access corridor and atrium, and hydrants are available at the atrium floor and adjoining upper floors.
items.ref: [NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex F, Cl. F-1, Fig. 16]
items.guide: Ceiling sprinklers are not required where the atrium ceiling is more than 17 m above the floor.

items.req: Atrium smoke extraction provides 6 air changes per hour in business occupancy and 8 in hotels and assembly occupancy, with fans capable of operating at 250 deg C for 120 min and on emergency power.
items.guide: Air changes are calculated on the atrium volume for a height of 15 m from the top. Review the design report and test record; witness fan start on alarm.

items.req: Make-up air supply points are beneath the smoke layer at the lower levels, and make-up air velocity does not exceed 1.02 m/s where it could contact the plume.
items.guide: Make-up air at 85 to 95 percent of the exhaust flow rate is recommended (F-1(j)).

items.req: Combustible waste, packaging and stored goods are not allowed to accumulate in plant rooms, service shafts, under stairs, on terraces or in basements.
items.ref: [Good practice; see NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex D, Cl. D-9.7(a); Cl. 3.4.6.3, 3.4.8.2.4]
items.guide: NBC specifically prohibits storage in substations and AHU rooms and requires housekeeping inspections in the fire prevention programme. Record locations and quantities.

items.req: An assembly point is designated outside the building, signed, kept clear and known to occupants.
items.ref: [Good practice; see NBC 2016, Part 4, Annex D, Cl. D-9.11]
items.guide: The Personal Fire Instruction Card format includes the assembly point. Check it is clear of fire tender routes and large enough for the occupant load.

items.req: Smoking is controlled, with designated areas and safe disposal of smoking materials.
items.guide: Check signage and evidence of smoking in stores, plant rooms, basements and staircases.

items.req: Temporary wiring, overloaded socket outlets, extension boards and portable heating or cooking appliances are controlled.
items.ref: [Good practice; see NBC 2016, Part 4, Cl. 3.4.6.1; CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 14, 23]
items.guide: Cross-refer to the electrical safety audit. Record locations.

items.req: Every person who operates or works on electrical lines and apparatus is designated by the owner/consumer, holds a certificate of competency or electrical work permit issued by the Appropriate Government, and is entered in a record (paper or electronic) of designated persons stating the purpose of designation.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 3(1) to (3), 4; Sch. II Form II, item 1]
items.guide: Ask for the register of designated persons. For each electrician / maintenance technician on the roster (in-house and AMC), check the name is in the register, the purpose is stated, and a valid competency certificate or wiring permit is on file. Record anyone working on panels who is not in the register.

items.req: An Electrical Safety Officer with the required qualification (degree in Electrical Engineering and 5 years O&M experience, or diploma and 10 years) is designated for the installation.
items.app: Installations (including factories) with connected load above 250 kW
items.guide: Obtain the connected load from the sanction letter or bill. Above 250 kW, check the written designation of the ESO and his qualification and experience certificates. See the Ambiguities sheet on whether the 250 kW limb applies to non-factory premises.

items.req: The Electrical Safety Officer inspects the installation and carries out the recommended periodic tests at intervals not exceeding one year, records them in the Schedule II forms, and keeps test reports and a register of safety recommendations acknowledged by the owner with the compliance made.
items.app: Where an Electrical Safety Officer is required
items.guide: Check the last two annual inspection records (Form I / II / III / IV), the test reports and the recommendations register. Every recommendation should show owner acknowledgement, action taken and date. An interval longer than 12 months is NC.

items.req: The installation has a current periodic inspection: by the Electrical Inspector where above the notified voltage, or self-certified by the owner and the report submitted in the Schedule II form where at or below it; the interval is as directed by the Appropriate Government and not more than five years; defects pointed out by the Inspector are rectified within the time given.
items.guide: Obtain the last Electrical Inspector certificate or self-certification report with its acknowledgement (deemed received if not acknowledged within 3 working days). Confirm the state's notified voltage and inspection periodicity (not in project files). Check every defect listed has been closed.

items.req: Installation work (other than like-for-like replacement of lamps, fans, fuses, switches and fittings at 250 V or less) is done only by a State-licensed electrical contractor under a certificate-of-competency holder; additions and alterations are not energised until approved by the Electrical Inspector or self-certified; supply is not recommenced after six months' disconnection without testing.
items.guide: Review work orders for fit-out, re-layout and panel changes since the last audit. Check the contractor licence number and supervisor's competency certificate, and the self-certification / approval for each alteration. Unrecorded new circuits or DBs found on site are NC.

items.req: Electric supply lines and apparatus are of adequate rating for power, insulation and fault current, conform to the relevant standards, show no sign of overloading, and are maintained and operated free from danger as recommended by the manufacturer.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 14(1), (3); Reg. 32(8); Reg. 48(7); Sch. II Form I/II, item on Reg. 14]
items.guide: Look for discoloured or melted insulation, hot or humming breakers, oversized fuses or breakers on undersized cables, and non-ISI devices. Cross-refer to thermography (hotspots), load current against breaker rating and cable size. Record overloaded circuits with readings.

items.req: All electrical equipment is installed above the highest flood level, or protected so that there is no water seepage, leakage or logging at the equipment.
items.guide: Check panel rooms, UPS and battery rooms, basements and areas below AC units, pipes and drains. Record any water stains, drips from AHU / FCU lines over or near panels, and equipment on the floor in areas that flood.

items.req: There is no unauthorised temporary installation; flexible cables for portable or transportable apparatus are insulated for the working voltage, protected against mechanical damage, three-core (single phase) or four-core (three phase) with an identifiable earth core, and any metallic covering is earthed.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 23; Sch. II Form I/II, item on Reg. 14(iv)]
items.guide: Walk the floor, back-of-house and display areas. Record two-core flex on metal-bodied equipment, joints taped in flexible cords, temporary or plastic cables used for CT / metering / PA supply, and cables run across floors without protection. See also O-04.

items.req: The supplier's service line, meter and cut-out / circuit breaker on the premises are in a safe condition, housed in an enclosed fire-proof receptacle in an accessible position, and not interfered with by the consumer.
items.guide: Inspect the incoming service, meter box and supplier's cut-out. Record broken covers, open enclosures, combustible boxes housing the cut-out, storage against it, or signs of tampering.

items.req: A linked switch, switch-fuse unit or circuit breaker (circuit breaker where supply is 11 kV and above) of adequate capacity is installed as near as possible to the point of commencement of supply, readily accessible and able to isolate the whole installation.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 16(2); Reg. 37(2); Sch. II Form II, item 17(i)]
items.guide: Locate the main incomer. Check it isolates all phases, is labelled, is reachable without moving goods or unlocking third-party rooms, and that staff on each shift know where it is.

items.req: Every distinct circuit is protected by a fuse or circuit breaker of adequate breaking capacity that will not cause danger from overheating, arcing or scattering of hot metal; each motor or apparatus has an adjacent, readily accessible linked switch, circuit breaker or emergency trip with manual reset.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 37(4), (5); Sch. II Form II, item 17(ii), (iii)]
items.guide: Check DB schedules against the breakers fitted. Record rewired or bridged fuses, breakers of breaking capacity below the prospective fault level, and motors (AHU, pumps, compressors) with no local isolator.

items.req: The earthed neutral conductor is permanently identified (IS colour code) and distinguishable from live conductors; switches are on the live conductors; no fuse, link, switch or breaker is inserted in the neutral other than a linked device that operates simultaneously on neutral and phases.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 17; Sch. II Form II, item 5]
items.guide: Open DBs (with a designated person). Check colours of phase, neutral and earth conductors, single-pole switching in the neutral, and neutral links. Socket polarity tests showing phase-neutral reversal, and TPN / DP devices with a damaged neutral pole, are NC.

items.req: A suitable earthed terminal is provided at the point of commencement of supply; where the installation exceeds 250 V the consumer also has an independent earthing system with its own electrode, interlinked with the supplier's earthed terminal through a link; both are protected against mechanical damage.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 18(1), (2); Sch. II Form II, item 6]
items.guide: Trace the main earth terminal at the incomer and the consumer's own earth electrode(s) and link. In multi-tenant buildings, confirm which earth pits serve the tenant and obtain their test reports.

items.req: Bare conductors in the building are inaccessible to the public with readily accessible switches to make them dead, and no live parts are exposed so as to cause danger.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 19; Reg. 37(7); Sch. II Form II, items 7, 17(iv)]
items.guide: Look for open DB doors with exposed busbars, missing blanking plates, missing panel covers or screws, exposed connectors on displays, and damaged sockets or switches. Any live part reachable by the public is a Critical finding.

items.req: A permanent danger notice in Hindi or English and the local language, with the skull and bones sign to the relevant standard, is fixed on every motor, generator, transformer and other electrical plant and its control apparatus (or on its enclosure).
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 20; Sch. II Form II, item 8]
items.guide: Check main LT panel, DBs, UPS, DG, transformer and motor starters. Record missing, faded or English-only notices where the local language is not English. Design benchmark: IS 2551 (not in project files).

items.req: All non-current-carrying metal parts of switchgear and control panels are earthed; insulating mats or floors of the appropriate voltage grade are provided in front of and behind panels where operation, maintenance or testing is done; every panel is identified by painted description at front and rear.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 21(5), (6); Sch. II Form II, item 9]
items.guide: Check panel body earthing, mats (ISI marked, voltage class marked, not cracked, covering the full working area front and rear) and panel name painted or permanently labelled on both faces. Benchmark for mats: IS 15652 (not in project files).

items.req: Persons working on electric supply lines or apparatus are provided with PPE, tools and devices suitable for the working voltage (rubber gloves, safety footwear, helmet, voltage detector / line tester, earthing devices, insulated hand tools and arc-flash protection), conforming to standards and kept in sound condition.
items.guide: Inspect the PPE kit at the panel room. Check glove voltage class and test date, footwear, face shield, voltage detector function and insulated tools. A kit with gloves only is PC; no kit is NC.

items.req: Before work on any conductor or apparatus it is isolated from all sources, proved dead, discharged and earthed, and protected against re-energisation (permit-to-work and lock-out / tag-out); hazards are identified and the team briefed; no lone working; the supervisor stays at the work spot.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 21(1), (3); Sch. I, Part II]
items.guide: Ask for the written isolation / permit-to-work procedure, locks and tags, and recent permits. Ask a technician to describe an isolation. No procedure or no LOTO devices is NC.

items.req: Circuits at different voltages, or at the same voltage, are readily distinguishable by permanent indication; installations with more than one feed (mains, DG, UPS, solar) are permanently marked so each source is identifiable.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 26; Reg. 27; Sch. II Form II, item 12]
items.guide: Check labels on DBs and outgoing feeders (raw power, UPS power, DG backed, solar) and on sockets. Record unlabelled feeders and DB ways.

items.req: Circuits and apparatus are arranged so that no part can become accidentally charged above its intended voltage; AC and DC circuits on the same box or support are segregated; where two supplies are not meant to run in parallel (mains / DG / solar / UPS bypass), the changeover is interlocked against paralleling and back-feed.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 28; Reg. 47(1)(iii); Sch. II Form II, items 13, 21]
items.app: Where more than one source of supply exists
items.guide: Check the changeover (AMF / ATS / manual) for mechanical and electrical interlock; test with the facility team where safe. Check DC battery and AC cabling segregation in UPS rooms.

items.req: Fire buckets filled with clean dry sand, conspicuously marked, are kept with suitable fire extinguishers; extinguishers are installed, maintained, inspected and tested with records; marked first-aid boxes are kept under the charge of a trained first-aider; locations of these are displayed in the control room / operator cabin.
items.app: Generating stations (including captive DG installations), enclosed substations and enclosed switching stations
items.guide: Check sand buckets (full, dry, marked), CO2 / clean agent extinguishers suited to electrical fires, first-aid box contents and the named first-aider for each shift. Extinguisher maintenance detail: see I-41 to I-45.

items.req: At least two gas masks are provided in accessible, conspicuous places for use in fire or smoke.
items.app: Generating stations of 5 MW and above; enclosed substations of 5 MVA and above
items.guide: Check number, location, condition and expiry of canisters or breathing apparatus.

items.req: The address and telephone number of the nearest doctor, a hospital with facilities for electric shock and burn treatment, ambulance and fire service are displayed near the electric shock treatment chart in the control room and operator cabin.
items.app: Generating stations, substations and switching stations (good practice at main panel rooms elsewhere)
items.guide: Check the display is current (call one number) and legible.

items.req: Instructions for resuscitation of persons suffering electric shock, in English or Hindi and the local language (English and Hindi where Hindi is the local language), are displayed conspicuously, and designated persons are competent to apply them.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 30(1), (2); Sch. II Form II, item 15]
items.app: Generating stations, enclosed substations, factories, and other premises where directed by the Electrical Inspector (good practice at all main panel rooms)
items.guide: Check the chart at the main panel / substation. Ask designated persons for CPR / first-aid training records and to describe the response to an electric shock.

items.req: Insulation resistance between conductors and earth is measured and recorded in megohms; a line disconnected for addition, alteration or repair is not reconnected until the insulation resistance test is done.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 35(1); Reg. 36; Reg. 42; Sch. II Form I/II]
items.guide: Obtain the latest IR test results for main feeders and DBs. Benchmark (auditor's, from IS 732 practice): not less than 1 megohm at 500 V DC for LV circuits; record lower values as findings. Check IR tests were done after recent alterations.

items.req: Test instruments used for installation testing are calibrated by a Government-authorised or NABL-accredited laboratory at the periodicity they specify.
items.guide: Check calibration certificates of the earth tester, insulation tester, loop impedance / RCD tester and clamp meter used by the maintenance team or contractor (and the audit team's own instruments).

items.req: An isolating device with cut-out or breaker on all phases (except neutral) is provided at the point of commencement of supply, in a conspicuous position not more than 1.70 m above ground, to isolate the whole building in an emergency.
items.app: Buildings above 15 m; airports, hospitals, hotels, places of entertainment and worship, cultural centres, stadia, academic buildings, test labs, industrial installations, premises with explosive or flammable material, railway / metro stations and other public buildings
items.guide: Measure the operating height of the emergency isolator, check it is signed and unobstructed, and that it isolates all phases. Ask the facility team when it was last operated.

items.req: Fire Retardant Low Smoke and Low Halogen (FRLS) power cables are used; Halogen Free Flame Retardant cables are used in airports, hospitals and hotels irrespective of height.
items.app: Buildings above 15 m (HFFR: airports, hospitals and hotels of any height)
items.guide: Read the cable sheath printing on risers, main feeders and recent extensions; check purchase records. Record non-FRLS cable runs with locations.

items.req: Distribution of electricity to the floors is by bus bar trunking.
items.app: Buildings above 15 m and other premises listed in Reg. 38(3)
items.guide: Check the rising mains. Existing cable risers installed before June 2023 should be reported as an observation with the date of installation.

items.req: Lightning protection of the building is provided as per the relevant standards, and its down conductors and earth terminations are inspected and tested.
items.app: Buildings above 15 m and other premises listed in Reg. 38(3)
items.guide: Check air terminals, down conductors, test joints and earth pits; obtain the last test report. Benchmark: IS/IEC 62305 (not in project files). Routing of down conductors: see G-20.

items.req: Electrical wiring of the building has been verified as per the relevant standards, and not less than 30 days' notice was given to the Electrical Inspector before supply was commenced or recommenced after six months.
items.app: Buildings above 15 m and other premises listed in Reg. 38(3)
items.guide: Obtain the wiring verification / test report (initial or periodic) and the Inspector's approval or notice. Benchmark: IS 732 verification (not in project files).

items.req: Conductors (other than overhead lines) are enclosed in mechanically strong, electrically continuous, earthed metal casing or covering (non-metallic conduit to standard permitted up to 650 V), unless accessible only to designated persons; all metal work enclosing or supporting the installation is earthed.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 39(i), (ii); Sch. II Form II, item 11]
items.guide: Check cable trays, conduits, trunking and glands. Record broken conduits, open cable entries without glands, unsupported cables and cable trays laid on the floor.

items.req: A clear space of not less than 1 m is kept in front of every switchboard; the space behind is either less than 20 cm or more than 75 cm, and where more than 75 cm there is a passage from either end clear to a height of 1.8 m.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 39(iii); Sch. II Form II, item 18]
items.guide: Measure with a tape. Record goods, furniture, TVs, cartons or cleaning equipment that reduce the 1 m front clearance, and rear spaces between 20 and 75 cm.

items.req: Where flammable materials (gases, liquids, chemicals) are produced, handled or stored, electrical equipment is flameproof, dust-tight, totally enclosed or otherwise suitable for the hazardous zone as per the relevant standards.
items.app: Where flammable materials are present (fuel stores, DG day tank rooms, paint / aerosol / gas stores)
items.guide: Obtain the hazardous area classification, if any. Check fittings, switches and sockets in these areas for Ex marking. Ordinary fittings in a classified zone are NC.

items.req: The neutral of every three-phase four-wire system is earthed; the neutral of every generator and transformer is earthed by not less than two separate and distinct connections; frames of generators, motors, transformers and other apparatus above 250 V are earthed by two separate and distinct connections.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 43(i), (vii), (xiii); Sch. II Form II, item 19(i)]
items.guide: Check DG, transformer and motor frames for two independent earth leads to the earth bar / pits. A single earth lead is NC.

items.req: All metal casings and coverings of cables and apparatus are earthed and bonded across junction boxes; every building has protective equipotential bonding of exposed and extraneous conductive parts.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 43(v), (viii); Sch. II Form II, item 19(ii), (vi)]
items.guide: Check gland earthing (copper, tight), conduit and tray bonding, and bonding of water, gas and structural metalwork at entry. Request the bonding test record.

items.req: In new or renovated installations, all plug sockets are three-pin and the third pin is permanently and effectively earthed.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 43(viii), second proviso; Sch. II Form I, item 5(ii)]
items.app: Installations at 250 V or less that are new or renovated
items.guide: Test a sample of sockets with a socket / earth continuity tester (all sockets in panel, UPS, staff and display areas). Record each failed socket by location and DB way.

items.req: Earthing systems use bonding conductors able to carry the prospective earth fault current, are mechanically strong and corrosion resistant, keep continuity through the life of the installation, and were tested for effective bonding before energisation.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 43(ix); Sch. II Form II, item 19(iv)]
items.guide: Inspect earth pits, strips and main earth bar. Record rusted strips, loose or bolted-only joints, earth wires that are damaged or undersized (for example a 10 mm2 cable used in place of an earth strip).

items.req: Earth fault loop impedance is tested at the origin of the installation, for each circuit and for all sources, and is low enough for the protective device to disconnect before touch voltage becomes harmful; results are recorded.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 43(x) to (xii); Sch. II Form II, item 19(vii) to (ix)]
items.guide: Obtain loop impedance test results. Compare each value with the maximum permitted for the protective device type and rating (IS 732 tables, not in project files). Absence of any loop impedance test is NC.

items.req: Earth resistance of each earth electrode is tested on a dry day in the dry season at least once a year, and the results are recorded and kept.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 43(x); Reg. 50(8); Sch. II Form I/II, item 19(iii), (v)]
items.app: All (annual test is explicit for supplier systems and for installations above 650 V; for LV consumers the Schedule II forms require the tested value and records)
items.guide: Obtain the last test report for every pit serving the premises, with date and value. CEA sets no ohmic limit; see the Ambiguities sheet for the benchmark. In multi-tenant buildings, obtain the landlord's report.

items.req: Use of electricity is controlled by a residual current device of rated residual current and operating time as per the relevant standards (not more than 30 mA in domestic installations), and RCDs are tested periodically.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 44; Sch. II Form II, item 20]
items.guide: Check RCD / RCCB / ELCB presence at the incomer and on socket and lighting circuits; note ratings. Press the test button with the facility team and record trip / no-trip. See the Ambiguities sheet for the non-domestic rating benchmark.

items.req: Installations above the notified voltage are inspected and approved in writing by the Electrical Inspector before commencement (or recommencement after six months); those at or below the notified voltage but above 650 V are self-certified; manufacturer's test certificates and site tests per standards are available for new or reconnected apparatus.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 45(1) to (6); Reg. 48(1) to (4)]
items.app: Where the premises own HV (above 650 V) installations
items.guide: Obtain the Inspector's approval letter / self-certification for the substation and each later addition, routine test certificates of transformers and switchgear, and site commissioning test reports.

items.req: HV apparatus, cables and supply lines are kept healthy with periodic tests as per the relevant standards, and records of all tests, trippings, maintenance and repairs are kept so that they can be compared with past records.
items.app: Where the premises own HV (above 650 V) installations
items.guide: Check transformer oil BDV / DGA (where oil filled), IR and tan-delta records, breaker maintenance, relay testing and the tripping register. Trend the results across at least two cycles.

items.req: HV conductors and apparatus are inaccessible except to designated persons; the supplier's apparatus and metering are in a separate locked, weather-proof and fire-proof enclosure or segregated; live parts within reach are protected; safety clearances allow easy operation and maintenance and ventilation; there is no encroachment below the installation.
items.app: Where the premises own HV (above 650 V) installations
items.guide: Inspect the HT room / yard: locks, signage, barriers, clearance around RMU / VCB / transformer, and storage or occupation beneath or around the installation.

items.req: A substation in a basement has its transformer room in the first basement at the periphery, with direct access from outside, surrounding walls of 4 h fire rating, 2 h fire doors kept closed with a notice to that effect, a curb at the entrance against oil flow, cable openings sealed to at least 2 h at all floors and walls, and FRLS cables.
items.app: Where a substation or switching station is located in a basement
items.guide: Check walls and doors (fire rating certificates), door closer and notice, curb height, cable sealing and cable type. CEA requires 4 h walls where NBC Cl. 3.4.6.3.2 (G-17) requires 120 min; apply the stricter value (see Ambiguities).

items.req: Oil-filled installations: no substation with apparatus holding more than 2 000 litre of oil is in a basement without proper oil draining; above 2 000 litre, fire barrier walls and an oil soak pit are provided (drainage where any tank exceeds 9 000 litre); spare oil is not stored near oil-filled equipment; oil-filled transformers indoors in other than residential or commercial buildings are on the ground floor or not below the first basement.
items.app: Where oil-filled transformers, switchgear or capacitors are installed
items.guide: Obtain oil quantities from nameplates. Check soak pit (clean, with stone fill), drain, barrier walls and storage of oil drums. Separation distances and 10 MVA spray protection: see G-16.

items.req: Only dry type transformers are used inside residential and commercial buildings.
items.app: Residential and commercial buildings with transformers inside the building
items.guide: Check transformer nameplates. An oil-filled transformer inside a residential or commercial building is NC (see also G-17).

items.req: HV substations have adequate fire detection and protection arrangements; cable trenches are filled with sand, pebbles or similar non-inflammable material or fully covered with non-inflammable slabs; underground substations have ventilation and drainage; spaces housing switchgear are not used for storage.
items.app: Where the premises own HV (above 650 V) installations
items.guide: Inspect detection, extinguishers / suppression, trench covers and fill, ventilation, drainage and housekeeping. Storage in the switch room: see also G-12.

items.req: HV interlocks are provided and working: isolator with its circuit breaker; earth switch with its isolator; breakers of supplies not meant to run in parallel; secondary breaker tripping with primary breaker of paralleled transformers; doors giving access to live parts.
items.app: Where the premises own HV (above 650 V) installations
items.guide: Witness interlock checks during a planned shutdown or review the last interlock test record. A defeated interlock is a Critical finding.

items.req: Protection is provided: over-current and earth fault on all circuits; a circuit breaker on the transformer primary for 1 000 kVA and above and on every transformer secondary; Buchholz, pressure relief and winding / oil temperature alarm and trip on transformers of 1 000 kVA and above; differential protection at 10 MVA and above; earth fault protection on generators of 100 kVA and above; REF or differential on generators of 1 000 kVA and above.
items.app: Where the premises own transformers or generators of the ratings stated
items.guide: Check relay schedules, settings and last secondary-injection test reports. Check DG earth fault (and REF where 1 000 kVA and above) in the AMF / DG panel.

items.req: The HV earthing system or mat limits touch and step potential and earth potential rise to tolerable values and keeps earth resistance low enough for protection to operate; transformer and generator neutrals are earthed by two separate connections; earth resistance is tested annually on a dry day and recorded.
items.app: Where the premises own HV (above 650 V) installations
items.guide: Obtain the earth mat design / test report and annual earth resistance records. Check two neutral earth leads per transformer and DG.

items.req: Outdoor substations (other than pole-type, or apparatus fully metal-enclosed with armoured cable connections) are fenced to not less than 1.8 m, and the fence is earthed.
items.app: Where an outdoor substation is provided
items.guide: Measure fence height, check gate locks, signage and fence earthing. Pole-type platforms: handrail, earthed if metal.

items.req: Every static capacitor (including APFC panels) has an arrangement for its immediate automatic or manual discharge on disconnection of supply.
items.app: Where static capacitors / APFC panels are installed
items.guide: Check discharge resistors or reactors are fitted and the warning on the panel. Ask for the capacitor maintenance record.

items.req: Luminous tube sign installations above 650 V: live parts screened and inaccessible; secondary earthed at the transformer and transformer cores earthed; dedicated primary sub-circuit; ELCB on the LV side; external signs have a conspicuous fire-proof linked emergency switch not more than 1.70 m above ground; a caution notice on every enclosure; 14 days' notice to the Electrical Inspector before use.
items.app: Where neon / luminous tube signs above 650 V are installed
items.guide: Check external signage transformers, the fireman's switch location and height, enclosures and notices. Not applicable to LED signage at low voltage.

items.req: Rooftop and ground solar PV: clear pathways of at least 75 cm with handrails for roof access and emergency exit and walkways between rows; DC disconnectors in combiner boxes readily accessible; a manual AC isolation switch outside the AC combiner box; AC phases and DC positive / negative colour coded; inverter at the building periphery near the panels; DC cables UV protected; ground-mounted arrays fenced to 1.8 m.
items.app: Where a solar PV installation serves the premises
items.guide: Walk the roof. Measure pathway widths, check handrails, isolators, labels and cable protection. Record DC cables lying loose on the roof.

items.req: Solar PV protection and earthing: inverter frame earthed to the earth bus by flexible braided copper; all array structures, enclosures and equipment earthed, with earth strips welded (not bolted) and interconnected earth pits; lightning arresters; surge protective devices with arc-extinguishing capability in every combiner box; over-current protection on combiner inputs and isolation on outputs; earth fault and insulation monitoring; fire detection and automatic suppression per standards.
items.app: Where a solar PV installation serves the premises
items.guide: Inspect earthing and SPDs; obtain the solar commissioning and earth test reports. Rusted or bolted earth strips are NC.

items.req: EV charging: each charging point on a dedicated sub-circuit with over-current protection in a switchboard; separate overload protection of input and output; socket-outlets at least 800 mm above finished ground; no extension leads, adaptors or portable socket-outlets; cable not more than 5 m to the vehicle; lightning protection; protection against reverse power flow; four-core cable for three-phase charging points; underground cables at least 1 m deep under vehicle passages.
items.app: Where EV charging points are installed
items.guide: Inspect each charger and its feeder. Measure socket height and cable length; check the DB for a dedicated breaker and RCD per charger.

items.req: EV charging: earth continuity monitoring that disconnects supply if the vehicle earth connection fails; protective earth conductor to the vehicle; charging lead with earthed metal shielding; enclosure of fire-retardant, self-extinguishing, halogen-free material; fire detection and alarm; RCD and charger tests as per the manufacturer; records of design, test certificates and inspections kept for at least seven years.
items.ref: [CEA Safety Regs 2023, Reg. 125(3) to (5); Reg. 126; Reg. 127; Reg. 128]
items.app: Where EV charging points are installed
items.guide: Check the charger data sheet for earth continuity monitoring, the RCD test record, fire detection coverage of the charging bay and the records file.
